On A4 and other sheet sizes, Print goes straight to your browser's print window, which has its own preview. See also [the thermal print preview](https://billing.reazix.com/help/thermal-printing.html#print-preview).

The line under the title names the paper, such as **A4 — click Print to send to your printer**.

| Control | What it does |

| Zoom slider, − and + | Make the preview smaller or bigger, from 30% to 250%. − and + step 10% at a time. It opens at 70% for A4 so the whole page fits, and 160% for a narrow receipt so you can read it; on a smaller window or a phone it opens smaller, so the whole width of the page fits. Zoom only changes this preview: the print is always full size on the chosen paper. |

| The percentage (such as 70% ) | Click it to go back to the normal size. |

| Download PDF | Only when opened from the invoice screen. Saves and downloads the PDF instead of printing, the same as [Save & Download](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#save-download). |

| Cancel , ✕ or Esc | Close it without printing. A click outside the window also closes it. |

| Print | Closes the preview and sends the invoice to print, then your browser's print window opens: choose the printer and click Print there. The button shows "Sending…" while it works. From the Dashboard this works like ⋯ **Print**: the print count goes up by one. |

**Something wrong?**
The preview looks right but the paper is cut off or tiny: check the paper size in the browser's print window matches your paper, with scale at 100% and margins at Default. Settings for paper, margins and design are in [Print and PDF settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/print-settings.html). Nothing happens on Print: see [Print does nothing](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked). Something missing on the page: see [Something is missing on the PDF](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#missing-on-pdf).

## Sending an invoice by WhatsApp or email

**WhatsApp** (in the ⋯ menu) sends a message with the invoice number, date and due date, client, total, what is paid or still due (or "FULLY PAID"), the status, and your business name.

- **On a phone or tablet** (Chrome or Safari): the app makes the PDF and opens your phone's share menu with it attached. Pick WhatsApp and the client.
- **On a computer**: WhatsApp does not let any website attach a file. So the client's chat opens in a new tab with the message, using the phone number saved for them, and the PDF is downloaded to your Downloads folder. Drag that PDF into the chat and send. If no number is saved, choose the contact in WhatsApp yourself.

**Email** opens your email program (Outlook, Windows Mail, Gmail if set as your mail app) with the subject **Invoice INV/0012 - ₹11,800**, a short "Dear …" message with the same details, and the client's email address filled in when the invoice or the saved client has one. Email links cannot attach files, so attach the PDF yourself: download it first with Save & Download on the invoice screen, or tick the invoice and use One merged PDF.

**Something wrong?**
Email does nothing: no email program is set as the default on this computer. Set one in Windows Settings, Apps, Default apps, Email, or copy the details into Gmail yourself. WhatsApp opens the wrong chat or says the number is invalid: save the client's phone with the country code, such as +91 98765 43210, in [Clients](https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html#client-form). For sending from the invoice screen, see [Sharing on WhatsApp](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#whatsapp).

## Cancelling an invoice

Under GST an invoice number, once issued, must stay in your books, so an issued invoice is **cancelled**, never deleted. Cancel one that was made by mistake, or for a sale that did not happen. (If goods came back after a real sale, issue a [credit note](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#credit-note) instead.)

- **Choose Cancel invoice**In the ⋯ menu on the row, click **Cancel invoice**. (Choosing **Cancelled** in the status dropdown does the same at once, without asking.)
- **Confirm**The window **Cancel this invoice?** explains what happens, and that you can undo it with the Undo cancel arrow among the row's actions. Click Cancel invoice to go ahead, or close it to keep the invoice.
- **Done**You see "Invoice cancelled & stock restored". The row shows **Cancelled** in grey.

A cancelled invoice keeps its number but no longer counts in totals, reports or GST returns, and any stock it used goes back. If you saved or printed its PDF, the copy in the Saved Invoices folder gets **CANCELLED** across every page. It is never shown as overdue, and cannot take a payment.

**To undo it**, click the Undo cancel arrow among the row's actions and answer **Yes, undo**. It goes back to Unpaid, Partial or Paid, from its payments, the stock is taken out again, and its saved PDF is put back exactly as it was.

**Something wrong?**
"A saved PDF could not be marked CANCELLED": that PDF is open in a PDF reader. Close it and cancel (or undo) again; see [Its PDF could not be updated](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#pdf-file-in-use). "Failed to cancel": nothing was changed; try again.

## Importing and exporting invoices as CSV

For moving many invoices in from Excel, Tally or another program, including **old invoices** from before you started using the app, or out to your CA, in one go. A CSV file is a plain spreadsheet file that Excel and Google Sheets can open and save.

- **Open it**Click CSV import / export at the top of the Dashboard. The window **Sales invoices: CSV import / export** opens.
- **Start from the template**Template downloads Sales-import-template.csv with the right columns and one example invoice of two items. Open it in Excel or Google Sheets, replace the example with your invoices, and save it as **CSV (Comma delimited)**.
- **Fill in your invoices**One row per item; an invoice of three items is three rows with the same invoice number. Write the client name and invoice date on each invoice's first row. The table below says what goes in each column. Save as CSV again when done.
- **Choose the two options****Take sold quantities out of product stock** (off to start): tick it for new sales; leave it off for old invoices whose stock you have already counted. **Add new clients to Clients** (on to start): clients not yet saved are added to your client list. A client is found by its **GSTIN** first: a row with a saved client's GSTIN goes to that client under its saved name, even if the name in the file is spelt differently, so no duplicate is made.
- **Choose the file**Choose CSV file reads it and shows what will happen **before** anything is saved: the file name, how many invoices are ready, how many already exist and will be skipped, how many new clients there are, any warning about dates, and every invoice with a problem.
- **Import**Click Import (it shows the number ready, such as **Import 25**). It says "Importing…" while it works, then a message such as "25 invoices imported · 2 already there, skipped". The list refreshes by itself.

Export all as CSV downloads every invoice of this business, oldest first, in the same columns as the template (cancelled invoices are left out), as Sales-invoices-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. You can edit that file and import it into another copy of the app.

**How to fill the file.** One row per item. Rows with the same invoice number make one invoice; give the client, date and other invoice details on the first row (later rows may leave them blank). Column names are matched loosely, so **Qty** or **Quantity**, **GSTIN** or **Client GSTIN**, **Customer** or **Client Name** all work. Dates can be 2026-10-01, 01-10-2026 or 01/10/2026 (day first, as in India).

| Column | What to put |

| Invoice Number, Invoice Date | Required. |

| Invoice Type | Tax Invoice (if blank), Bill of Supply, Composition, Quotation, Proforma, Delivery Challan or Credit Note. |

| Due Date | Optional. Needed for the invoice to become overdue. |

| Client Name, Client GSTIN, Client State, Client Address, Client Country | The name is required. A client already in Clients (same name) fills in the rest. The state can be a name (Maharashtra), a 2-digit GST state code (27), or left blank to take it from the GSTIN. |

| Place of Supply | Only if it differs from the client's state. It decides CGST + SGST (same state as you) or IGST (another state). |

| Item Name, HSN/SAC, Quantity, Unit, Rate | Item name and rate are required; quantity is 1 if blank. A product of the same name fills in a missing HSN or unit. |

| Discount | Rupees off that line. |

| GST %, Cess % | Such as 18 and 0. |

| Prices Include Tax | Yes if the rates already include GST. |

| Notes | Printed on the invoice. |

| Bill Discount, Round Off | For the whole invoice: rupees off after tax, and Yes to round the total to the rupee. |

GST, CGST + SGST or IGST and the totals are worked out exactly as on the invoice screen. Imported invoices start **Unpaid**, in rupees. An invoice number that already exists is **skipped, never overwritten**. Two different invoices with the same number (for example, numbering that restarts each year) are refused: give one of them its own number.

**Something wrong?**
Each problem names the row or invoice and what to fix, for example "Invoice INV/0101: row 3 has no item name." or "date "31/02/2026" is not a date". Invoices with problems are not imported; fix the file and choose it again (the good ones already imported are then skipped as "already there"). "The dates are month first": your Excel wrote US dates; change the date columns to DD-MM-YYYY. A file saved as .xlsx does not work, even if renamed: see [A CSV import did not work](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#csv-import). For purchase bills, use the same window on the Purchases screen: [Importing purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#csv-purchases).

## Printing many invoices as one PDF

The **Quick print** row above the list combines invoices into one PDF file, without ticking anything. It uses the list **as it is filtered now**, so set the filters first: for example From 1 October To 31 October, then All shown gives October's invoices for your CA.

| Button | Puts in the PDF |

| All shown (n) | Every invoice in the list |

| Unpaid only (n) | Only those marked Unpaid, not part-paid or overdue |

| Overdue (n) | Only overdue ones, for chasing payments |

| Paid (n) | Only fully paid ones |

The number in brackets is how many will go in. Each invoice starts on a new A4 page; a long one takes as many pages as it needs. For more than five invoices, a message shows how far it has got; for more than 100 you are asked first, as it can take a minute. The file reazix-invoices-25-2026-10-31.pdf lands in your Downloads folder, and a message says how many were included.

**Something wrong?**
"No overdue invoices to print": none in the list match; check the filters. "Could not generate any PDFs": see [Print does nothing, or "Print failed"](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked). To choose exactly which invoices go in, tick them and use One merged PDF or Separate PDFs (ZIP) instead (see below).

## Ticking several invoices

Tick the box at the start of each row, or the box in the header to tick every row in the list as filtered. For a set of dates, such as one month, fill in **From** and **To** in the filters first, then tick the header box. A blue bar appears above the list with how many are ticked, such as **3 selected**, and these buttons:

| Button | What it does |

| Mark paid , Mark unpaid , Mark overdue | Change them all, after asking. Mark paid records a payment for each balance (note "Marked paid (bulk)"); Mark unpaid takes such payments back, as the status dropdown does. Only tax invoices, bills of supply and composition bills change; ticked quotations or challans are left alone. Marking a cancelled invoice as anything brings it back and takes its stock out again. |

| Export JSON | Saves the ticked invoices to one file, such as reazix-bills-3-2026-10-31.json , which can be brought back with [Import](https://billing.reazix.com/help/backup.html#export-import) in Settings, Backup. |

| One merged PDF | Combines the ticked invoices into one PDF, one invoice per page, useful for your CA or for filing. Works like Quick print . |

| Separate PDFs (ZIP) | One PDF file per ticked invoice, named by its invoice number (such as INV-0012.pdf ), downloaded together in one ZIP, such as invoices-26-2026-10-31.zip . Open the ZIP to get the files. |

| E-invoice JSON | Only when e-invoicing is on. One file with the ticked invoices, to upload on the e-invoice portal. See E-invoicing from the Dashboard . |

| Set cost centre… | Only when [cost centres](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#cost-centres) are on. Tags the ticked invoices with one branch, site or project, after asking; **Remove cost centre** takes it off. Only the cost centre changes. |

| Cancel | Shows only while a PDF is being made. Stops after the current invoice and still saves the PDF of those done. |

| Cancel invoices | Cancels the ticked invoices, after asking, and puts their stock back. See Cancelling an invoice . |

| ✕ | Unticks everything. |

Changing any filter or the search clears the ticks, so you never act on invoices you can no longer see. When some fail to save, a message says how many were updated and how many failed; try those again.

## E-invoicing from the Dashboard

E-invoicing is only for businesses whose yearly turnover has crossed ₹5 crore: their B2B invoices must be registered on the government's e-invoice portal, which gives each one an **IRN** (Invoice Reference Number) and a signed QR code. If that is not you, leave it off. When **E-invoicing (IRN)** is on in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features), the Dashboard gets two extra buttons:

- **E-invoice JSON**Tick the invoices to register and click E-invoice JSON in the bar. A JSON file downloads with every invoice that passed the checks. Upload it on einvoice1.gst.gov.in (e-Invoice, Bulk Upload).
- **Import IRN**Download the result file from the portal, then click Import IRN at the top of the Dashboard and choose it. Each IRN is saved on the invoice with the same number, date and GSTIN, and you see "IRN saved on 3 invoices. It now prints on them." Nothing else on the invoice changes.

Invoices left out of the file, or IRNs that could not be matched, are listed in a window with what to fix for each (for example a client with no GSTIN, an item with no HSN code, or an invoice that already has an IRN). Fix them and export again. Registered invoices show a green **IRN** beside their number on the Dashboard. The full rules and checks are in [E-invoicing (IRN)](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#e-invoice).

**Something wrong?**
"No IRN was found in that file": you chose the file you uploaded, not the one the portal gave back. Download the portal's result as JSON and import that.

---

# Clients

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html

Everyone you bill, what each one owes, their account statement, and how quickly they pay.

## The client list

Clients in the sidebar opens a list of everyone you sell to. Use it to see at a glance who owes you money, to open one client's account, and to keep their address and GSTIN ready for the next invoice.

Every client you have saved, and every name you have ever invoiced, appears as a card. The clients who owe you the most are at the top, so the people to call first are always first.

The buttons at the top of the screen:

| Button | What it does |

| Import (Excel / CSV) | Adds many clients at once from a spreadsheet. See Importing clients . |

| Add Client | Opens the client form for a new client. See Adding and editing a client . |

| New Invoice | Opens a blank invoice. |

**Search clients...** finds a client by any part of the name, in small or capital letters. The cross clears the search. If nothing matches, or you have no clients yet, you see **No clients found.** and a Add Your First Client button.

Your client list is shared by all your businesses, since the same customer may buy from each.

### What a client card shows

| On the card | Meaning |

| Letter in a circle | The first letter of the name. |

| Name | The client's name, exactly as written on the invoices. |

| **N invoices** | state | GSTIN | How many sales and credit notes they have, then the state and GSTIN of a saved client. |

| **Total** | Everything you have billed them, less credit notes. |

| **Paid** (green) | What they have paid you on those invoices. |

| **Outstanding** (red) | What they still owe. TDS that the client deducted is not counted as owed, since they pay it to the government for you. Green ₹0 means all settled. |

| **Overpaid** (blue) | Shown instead of Outstanding when they paid more than they were billed. The extra can be used on [their next invoice](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#client-credit). |

| View / Hide | Click anywhere on the card to open or close the client's account. |

Only real sales count in these figures: Tax Invoices, Bills of Supply and Composition bills. Credit notes are subtracted. Quotations, proformas, delivery challans and cancelled invoices are left out, because nobody owes money on them.

### Names you invoiced but never saved

An invoice can go to a name that is not in your saved list, for example a walk-in customer. That name still gets a card, so you can see what they owe, but it shows no state or GSTIN. Open the card and click Save as Client at the bottom to save them: the form opens with the name filled in.

**Something wrong?****One client shows as two cards.** Cards are matched by name. "Sharma Traders" and "Sharma Traders Pvt Ltd" are two different names, so they make two cards. If you renamed a saved client, old invoices keep the name they were made with and stay on a card of their own. Small and capital letters do not matter.
**A client is missing.** Clear the search box. A client with no saved record and no invoices does not exist yet: add them with Add Client.

## Adding and editing a client

Save a client once and you never type their details again: on a new invoice, pick them from the list under **Client Name** and their address, state, GSTIN and preferences are filled in.

- **Open the form**Click Add Client at the top of the Clients screen. To change a saved client, open their card and click Edit Client. The same form opens from the invoice screen, from the pencil next to a saved client or when you save a new one there.
- **Fill in the name****Client / Business Name** is the only required field. Use the name you want printed on the invoice.
- **Address and state**Fill in the address, choose the country (it starts as your own) and the state. The state decides whether GST is CGST + SGST or IGST, so get it right.
- **GSTIN**For a registered business, type their 15-character GSTIN. When you click out of the box it is checked (see below).
- **Save**Click Save Client, or Update Client when editing. You see "Client added" or "Client updated" and the card appears in the list. Cancel or the cross at the top closes the form without saving.

The fields:

| Field | What to know |

| Client / Business Name * | Required. If it is blank, nothing is saved. |

| Address | Street address and locality, printed on the invoice. |

| Country | Starts as your own business's country. Changing it clears the state, since each country has its own list. A client outside India is billed as an export, charged as IGST: see [How GST is worked out](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#gst). |

| City | Printed with the address. |

| PIN Code | The label changes with the country, such as ZIP Code or Postcode. |

| State | A list for India; a text box for countries without a list. The label changes with the country too, such as Emirate or County. |

| GSTIN | The client's GST number. Leave it blank for an unregistered customer (a B2C sale). For other countries the box asks for their tax number, such as TRN or VAT Number. |

| Email | Used as the "To" address when you email an invoice from the client's account. |

| Phone | Used for WhatsApp. Write it with the country code, such as +91 98765 43210. |

| SEZ unit / Developer | India only. See SEZ clients . |

| Print preferences (optional) | Preferred paper size, currency and auto-print for this client. See Print preferences . |

Changing a client's details does not change invoices already made: each invoice keeps the details it was saved with. To correct one, open it, pick the client again under **Client Name**, and save.

### Clients abroad

Pick the client's country. For a country other than India:

- No GSTIN and no state are needed. The state box is marked optional, and the postal code box takes that country's name for it (ZIP Code, Postcode...).
- The tax ID box is named after their country's tax ID (VAT Number, EIN / TIN, TRN...). If the client gave you one, type it: it prints on the invoice with that name. It is optional.
- Their country prints under their address, and the place of supply prints as Outside India (country), because an export is supplied outside India.
- **Preferred currency** lists every currency the app knows. Left blank, invoices to them start in their country's currency. See [Billing in another currency](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#currency).

Billing such a client is an export: see [Exports and foreign clients](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-basics.html#exports) and [LUT](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-basics.html#lut).

### The GSTIN check

A GSTIN is the 15-character GST number of a registered business. Its first two digits are the state code (03 is Punjab, 27 is Maharashtra), the next ten are the PAN, and the last is a check character. When you click out of the GSTIN box, the app reads it. This works offline; nothing is looked up on the GST portal.

| What happens | Meaning |

| The State fills in by itself | The state was blank, so it was taken from the first two digits. |

| ⚠ GSTIN format looks unusual. Expected like: 22AAAAA0000A1Z5 | It is not 15 characters in the GSTIN pattern. Check for a missing or extra character, or the letter O typed for zero. |

| ⚠ This GSTIN fails its own checksum — check for a typo. | The pattern is right but the last character does not add up, so a character is almost certainly mistyped. |

| ⚠ This GSTIN is registered in state , but the state says other state . | Either the GSTIN or the state you chose is wrong. Check with the client. |

The box turns amber while there is a warning. Warnings never stop you saving. Small letters are turned into capitals as you type. The same check runs on the invoice: see [What the GSTIN check tells you](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#gstin-check).

### Why the state matters (place of supply)

The **place of supply** is where a sale is treated as happening for GST. For most sales it is the client's state:

- Client in **your own state**: the invoice charges **CGST + SGST** (half each).
- Client in **another state**, an SEZ, or abroad: the invoice charges **IGST**.

A wrong state on the client quietly gives the wrong tax on every invoice to them, and puts the sale in the wrong place in GSTR-1. If goods go somewhere other than the client's address, set **Place of Supply** on that invoice instead. See [How GST is worked out](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#gst) and the [glossary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms).

**Something wrong?**IGST where you expected CGST + SGST, or the other way round: check the client's state here, your own state in [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details), and the place of supply on the invoice. See [The invoice has the wrong tax split](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#wrong-tax).

### SEZ clients

Tick **SEZ unit / Developer** for a client in a Special Economic Zone. Supplies to them are charged IGST whatever their state, even if they are in your own state (section 16 of the IGST Act). The box only shows when the country is India.

### Print preferences

Some clients always want the same thing: a thermal receipt, an A5 bill, or an invoice in dollars. Set it once here and every new invoice for them starts that way. All three are optional; leave them blank to use your normal settings.

| Field | What it does |

| Preferred paper size | A4, A5, US Letter, 80mm or 76mm thermal and the other sizes. **Use app default** keeps your usual size. |

| Preferred currency | INR, USD, EUR, GBP, AED, SGD or AUD. **Use invoice default** keeps the invoice's normal currency. |

| Auto-print on save for this client | Sends the invoice to the printer each time you save one for this client, even if auto-print is off in [Print Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/print-settings.html#auto-print). |

They are applied when you pick this client on a new invoice. You can still change them on that invoice.

The app also learns: each time you save an invoice for a saved client, the paper size and currency that invoice used become the client's preferred ones. So if you change one invoice to thermal, the next one for that client starts as thermal too.

## A client's account

Click a client's card to open their account. It shows everything about this one client in one place.

From top to bottom:

- Statement PDF and Aging PDF: see Statement and ageing PDFs.
- The **Aging** strip, when they owe you anything: see Ageing.
- Their address, email and phone, if saved.
- All their invoices, newest first.
- Edit Client and Delete Client, or Save as Client.

A client with no invoices shows **No invoices for this client yet.** and a Create Invoice button.

### The invoice rows

Each row has the **Date**, **Invoice No.**, **Type** (Tax Invoice, Quotation, Credit Note and so on), **Amount**, **Status** and these buttons:

| Button | What it does |

| Edit Invoice (pencil) | Opens the invoice on the invoice screen to change it. |

| Duplicate Invoice | A new invoice with the same client and items, a new number and today's date. |

| WhatsApp | Opens WhatsApp with a short message: invoice number, amount, date and status. It goes to the phone number saved on that invoice. The PDF is not attached; send it from the invoice screen if you need it (see [WhatsApp](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#whatsapp)). |

| Email | Opens your email program with a message about the invoice, addressed to the client's saved email. |

| Delete Invoice (bin) | Asks first, then moves the invoice to the Trash for 30 days and puts its stock back. |

A row past its due date and not paid is highlighted as overdue.

Deleted by mistake? Restore it from [Settings, Trash bin](https://billing.reazix.com/help/backup.html#trash) within 30 days. For an invoice already given to the client, [cancel it](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#cancel) on the Dashboard instead of deleting, so its number stays in your records.

### Changing the status

The coloured box in the **Status** column is a dropdown: **Unpaid**, **Partial**, **Paid** or **Overdue**. It works as on the Dashboard:

- **Paid** records a payment for the rest of the balance, so the client's Paid and Outstanding update.
- **Unpaid** on a paid invoice takes back the payment that marking it Paid recorded. Payments you recorded yourself stay.
- **Partial** and **Overdue** only change the label. To record part of a payment with its amount and mode, use the ₹ button on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments).

A cancelled invoice shows **Cancelled** and cannot be changed here; undo the cancel from the Dashboard. See [Status](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#status).

### Edit, delete or save the client

| Button | What it does |

| Edit Client | Opens the client form with their details. |

| Delete Client | Asks **Remove this saved client?**, then removes them from your saved list. Their invoices stay untouched, and the name still shows as a card while it has invoices. You can add them again any time. |

| Save as Client | Shown instead of the two above for a name you invoiced but never saved. Opens the form with the name filled in. |

**Something wrong?****WhatsApp opens but not to the client's chat.** The phone number on the invoice needs the country code: 919876543210 or +91 98765 43210, not just 98765 43210. Fix it with Edit Client. For an invoice already made, open it, pick the client again under **Client Name** and save, so it carries the new number.
**Email opens with an empty "To".** The client has no email saved. Add it with Edit Client.

## Ageing: who is slow to pay

When a client owes you money, an **Aging** strip under the PDF buttons splits what they owe by how late it is:

| Group | Holds unpaid amounts that are |

| **Current** (green) | Not yet due, or up to 30 days past due |

| **31-60d** (amber) | 31 to 60 days late |

| **61-90d** (orange) | 61 to 90 days late |

| **90+ d** (red) | More than 90 days late. Call these first. |

Lateness is counted from the invoice's **due date**, or from the invoice date when it has none. Only unpaid sales are counted; TDS the client deducted is not. The strip is hidden when nothing is owed.

The strip adds up unpaid invoices one by one, and does not take credit notes off them. So if the client has a credit note, the strip can total more than **Outstanding** on the card.

To see ageing for all clients together, use [Reports, Outstanding](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#outstanding) or [Party Outstanding](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#party-outstanding).

## Statement and ageing PDFs

Two buttons at the top of an opened client make PDFs you can send them or keep. Each one downloads straight away, and you see "Statement PDF generated" or "Aging report for name downloaded". If you set your own PDF colours in [Print Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/print-settings.html#colours), the coloured bands and lines follow them.

### Statement PDF

The client's whole account, like a bank passbook. Send it when a client disputes a bill or asks "how much do I owe?". It contains:

- Your business (**FROM**) and theirs (**BILL TO**), with addresses and GSTINs.
- A summary: **Invoices**, **Total Billed**, **Paid** and **Outstanding**.
- A table with **Date**, **Particulars** (number and type), **Debit**, **Credit** and **Balance**, oldest first. Each invoice is a debit. Under it, what was paid against it shows as Payment recd against above, and TDS they deducted as TDS deducted by client, both as credits. A credit note is a credit.
- The running balance after each line, marked **Dr** (they owe you, in red) or **Cr** (you owe them, in green), and the **CLOSING BALANCE**.
- A line for your signature and a note asking them to confirm within 7 days.

It covers all their invoices, from an opening balance of zero. Quotations, proformas, challans and cancelled invoices are left out. Amounts print as "Rs." because the PDF font has no ₹ sign. The file is named like statement-Sharma-Traders-2026-10-29.pdf.

### Aging PDF

Only what is still unpaid, for collection calls. It lists each unpaid invoice with its **Invoice #**, **Date**, **Due** date, **Age** in days, **Total** and **Outstanding**. Amounts more than 60 days old are in red. Below the list, an **AGING SUMMARY** gives the four groups (0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days) and the **TOTAL OUTSTANDING**. The file is named like Aging-Sharma_Traders-2026-10-29.pdf.

**Something wrong?**"No invoices for this client" or "name has no outstanding balance.": there is nothing to put in that PDF. A paid-up client has no Aging PDF.
Nothing downloads: your browser may be asking where to save, or blocking downloads from the app. Allow downloads, then click again.
The balance looks wrong: check that each payment was recorded on the right invoice, and that quotations were converted into invoices. See [Recording a payment](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments).

## Importing clients from a spreadsheet

Moving from another program or an Excel list? Import (Excel / CSV) adds many clients at once, one per row.

- **Open the window**Click Import (Excel / CSV) on the Clients screen. The window **Import clients from Excel or CSV** opens.
- **Get the sample file**Click Download sample file. Clients-sample.csv lands in your Downloads folder, with the right column headings and two demo clients.
- **Fill it in**Open it in Excel or Google Sheets. Replace the demo rows with your clients, one per row. Keep the first row (the headings) as it is.
- **Save it**Save it as Excel (.xlsx or .xls) or as CSV: all of them work.
- **Choose the file**Click Choose file (Excel or CSV). Nothing is saved yet: the window shows how many clients are ready and how many are already in your list (skipped).
- **Import**Click Import (such as **Import 12**). You see "Imported 12 clients", and the new cards appear.

**Moving from MARG, Tally, Busy or Vyapar?** Export the party (ledger) list to Excel and choose that file as it is. Headings such as Party Name, Ledger Name, GSTIN/UIN, Mobile No, Address 1, Address 2 and City are understood. If the list has a Group column, only customers (Sundry Debtors) are added; suppliers, banks and expense ledgers are left out.

The columns (headings in small or capital letters, in any order):

| Column heading | Holds |

| Name (or Client , Client Name , Customer ) | Required. Rows without a name are skipped. |

| GSTIN | Optional. Leave blank for a client without GST. |

| Phone (or Mobile ), Email | Optional |

| Address | Optional |

| State | Optional. Write it in full, as in the app's list (Punjab, not PB). |

The sample file looks like this:

```
Name,GSTIN,Phone,Email,Address,State
Demo Traders,27AAAAA0000A1Z5,9800000001,accounts@demo-traders.example,"Shop 4, Demo Market, Pune",Maharashtra
Sample Studio,,9800000002,hello@sample-studio.example,"12 Sample Street, Kolkata",West Bengal
```

Clients you already have (same name, any capitals) are skipped, and so are repeats inside the file, so importing the same file twice is safe. Other columns, such as city or PIN, are ignored: add them later with Edit Client. Imported GSTINs are not checked; open the client and click into the GSTIN box and out again to check one.

**Old invoices** are imported on the Dashboard, with CSV import / export: it can add their clients to this list at the same time. See [Importing and exporting invoices as CSV](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#csv).

**Something wrong?**Nothing is read: the file is not a plain CSV, or the headings are not in the first row. An .xlsx file renamed to .csv does not work. See [A CSV import did not work](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#csv-import).
An address with a comma in it must be inside double quotes, "12, MG Road". Excel does this for you when it saves as CSV.

---

# Products and stock

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html

Save what you sell once, then pick it on every invoice. Stock goes down as you sell and up as you buy.

## The product list

Products in the sidebar opens your catalogue: the goods and services you sell or buy, with their prices, GST rate and stock. Save an item here once, and on every invoice you just type a few letters of its name to fill in the HSN, rate, unit and GST.

The buttons at the top of the screen:

| Button | What it does |

| Import (Excel / CSV) | Adds many products at once from a spreadsheet. See Importing products . |

| Bulk edit | Turns the list into a grid you can type in, to change many products at once. See Bulk edit . Greyed out until you have a product. |

| Make | Only when manufacturing is turned on: records goods you made from raw materials. See Manufacturing . |

| Add Product | Opens the product form. See Adding a product or service . |

**Search by name or HSN...** narrows the list as you type. The cross clears it.

The **Products & Services** table:

| Column | Shows |

| Name | The product name. Point at it to see its description. A product made from raw materials also shows **Made here · cost ₹… per unit** under its name. |

| HSN/SAC | Its HSN or SAC code, or a dash. |

| Rate | The selling price. |

| GST % | The GST rate. |

| Unit | Pcs, Kg, Hrs and so on. |

| Stock | How many you have. **Out of Stock** in red at zero or below; the number in amber when it is at or below your low-stock threshold . **Service** for a service , which has no stock, and a dash (-) for goods whose stock was never entered: neither is ever out of stock. |

| Actions | The pencil (**Edit**) opens the product form; the bin (**Delete**) deletes it after asking. |

Products are shared by all your businesses, so each business sees the same list and the same stock.

### Printing or exporting the list

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV beside the table title save the products shown, with name, type (Goods or Service), HSN/SAC, purchase price, selling price, GST %, unit and stock. Search first to save only some. Print / PDF opens the print window, where you can choose a printer or **Save as PDF**. The buttons are hidden during a bulk edit.

A CSV saved here can be opened in Excel, and is a handy way to send your price list to an accountant. It can also be brought back in with Import (Excel / CSV), or into another copy of the app.

### Deleting a product

The bin asks **Delete this product?** first. Deleting removes it from your catalogue only: invoices and purchase bills that used it keep their lines unchanged. If it is a raw material of a product made here, the message names those products: remove it from their raw materials list too.

A product deleted here is not in the Trash; to get it back, add it again.

## Adding a product or service

- **Open the form**Click Add Product. To change a product, click its pencil instead; the form opens as **Edit Product**.
- **Name it**Type the name as you want it printed on the invoice, such as "A4 Paper Ream 75 GSM" or "Website Maintenance".
- **Goods or service**Under **This is a**, leave **Goods (stock counted)** for things you keep on a shelf, or click **Service (no stock)** for work you do, such as printing, repairs or consulting. See Goods or service.
- **Codes and prices**Fill in the HSN or SAC code, the purchase price, the selling price and the GST %.
- **Unit and stock**Choose the unit and, for goods, type how many you have today. A service has no stock box.
- **Save**Click Save (or Update when editing). You see "Product added" or "Product updated", and it appears in the list.

Cancel closes the form without saving. So does clicking outside it, so finish and save before you click elsewhere.

| Field | What to know |

| Product / Service Name * | Required. Two products should not share a name: invoices, purchase bills and imports find products by name. |

| This is a | **Goods (stock counted)** (to start) or **Service (no stock)**. See Goods or service . |

| HSN / SAC Code | HSN for goods, SAC for services. For a service the box is labelled **SAC Code**. See HSN and SAC codes . |

| Purchase Price | What you pay the supplier for one unit. Filled in on new purchase bills, used to value your stock and to cost things you make. |

| Selling Price | What you charge for one unit. Filled in on new invoices, and shown as the **Rate** in the list. Type it the same way your invoices work: before GST, unless you make [tax-inclusive](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#tax-inclusive) invoices. |

| GST % | The GST rate, such as 5 or 18. 0 to 100; blank counts as 0. Since 22 September 2025 most goods are at 5%, 18% or 40%. |

| Unit | Pcs to start. Pcs, Nos, Kg, g, Tonne, Ltr, ml, Mtr, cm, Ft, In, Sq.ft, Sq.m, Hrs, Day, Week, Month, Year, Visit, Session, Project, Word, Page, Box, Dozen, Pair, Set, Bag, Roll, Bottle, and your own [custom units](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#items), marked ★. |

| Stock Quantity | Goods only. How many you have now. After this, sales and purchases change it for you; see How stock is counted . Left blank, the stock is **not counted**: the list shows a dash, never **Out of Stock**, until you type a number, buy it on a purchase bill or sell it. |

| Description (optional) | For your own reference. It shows when you point at the name in the list. |

| Made here (from raw materials) | Only when manufacturing is turned on. See Bill of materials . |

Changing a product's price or GST % does not change invoices already made. New invoices use the new figures.

**Something wrong?**"Product name is required": fill in the name. "GST % must be between 0 and 100": type just the number, such as 18, not 18% or 0.18.
A service shows **Out of Stock** in red: it was saved as Goods (all products made before version 1.10.83 are). Click its pencil, choose **Service (no stock)** and click Update.

### Goods or service

Every product is either **Goods**, things you buy, keep and sell, whose stock is counted, or a **Service**, work you do, such as printing, repairs, design, consulting or transport, which has no stock.

| | Goods (stock counted) | Service (no stock) |

| Stock box in the form | Yes | No |

| Selling it on an invoice | Takes the quantity out of stock | Moves no stock, and never says "out of stock" |

| Buying it on a purchase bill | Adds the quantity to stock | Moves no stock |

| Low-stock alerts, the bell, the Dashboard low-stock strip, the stock report | Included | Never included |

| Manufacturing | Can be a raw material or be made here | Neither |

| Code box | HSN / SAC Code | SAC Code |

| Unit list | Every unit | Service units first (Hrs, Day, Month, Project, Nos, Page...). A new service starts on Hrs; change it to whatever you bill by. |

| Stock column in the list | The count, or **Out of Stock** | **Service** |

**Products you already have** stay Goods. To switch one, click its pencil, choose **Service (no stock)** and click Update; any stock it had is dropped. To switch back, choose **Goods** and type its stock.

On an invoice, picking a service from your products fills in that line's SAC, unit, rate and GST; other lines are not touched. For a service billed as one fixed fee, with no quantity on the invoice, see [Goods, services or both](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#goods-services).

When importing products from a spreadsheet, a Type column with Service makes the row a service. See Importing products.

### HSN and SAC codes

**HSN** (Harmonised System of Nomenclature) codes classify goods, such as 4802 for paper or 8471 for computers. **SAC** (Services Accounting Code) codes classify services and start with 99, such as 998314 for IT services. The code decides the GST rate and is reported in your GSTR-1, in the HSN summary.

- Businesses with a turnover up to ₹5 crore must show at least a **4-digit** HSN on invoices to registered buyers; above ₹5 crore, **6 digits** on every invoice.
- Find your code on your supplier's bill, from your accountant, or with the HSN search on the GST portal.
- On the invoice, the app knows the usual GST rate of common codes and shows it under the HSN box. See [Line items](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#items).

See also the [glossary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms).

### Barcode

Give a product its barcode once, and scanning it on an invoice adds the product. See [Scanning barcodes on an invoice](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#scan-barcode).

- **Open the product**Click Add Product, or the edit button on a product in the list.
- **Click the Barcode box**Then scan the product's barcode with your scanner, or type the number printed under the bars.
- **Save**Click Save. Pressing Enter in the Barcode box does nothing else, so a scan never saves the form half filled.
- One barcode belongs to one product. Saving a code another product already has shows which product has it, and nothing is saved.
- The barcode is kept exactly as scanned, leading zeros included. Capital and small letters count as the same.
- The search box above the list finds products by barcode too.
- Bulk edit has a Barcode column, and Import reads a **Barcode** column (also called EAN, UPC, SKU or Item code). In Excel, format that column as **Text** first: otherwise Excel turns a long barcode into a number like 8.9E+12, and the import refuses that row.

## Bulk edit: changing many products at once

Use it when prices go up across the board, after a GST rate change, or to correct stock after counting your shelves. Bulk edit turns the table into a grid of boxes: **Name**, **HSN/SAC**, **Purchase price**, **Selling price**, **GST %**, **Unit** and **Stock**.

- **Narrow the list (optional)**Search first, for example by an HSN code, to edit only those products. The search box is locked while you edit.
- **Start**Click Bulk edit.
- **Type the changes**Change any boxes, in any rows. Each changed row turns blue, and the bar at the top counts them: "3 products changed".
- **Save once**Click Save changes (3). You see "3 products updated" and the normal list comes back.

Cancel drops every change. Only the boxes you changed are saved: if an invoice in another window sold some stock meanwhile, that is not undone (unless you changed that product's stock yourself).

The same rules as the product form apply: every product needs a name, GST % must be 0 to 100, and prices and stock must be numbers. If one row breaks a rule, **nothing** is saved and you are told which product to fix, such as "Not saved: Tea: GST % must be 0 to 100". Make and the export buttons wait until you save or cancel.

**Something wrong?**"2 saved, 1 failed. Try again.": the app could not reach its data for one product. Click Bulk edit again, check the product, and save it again.

## How stock is counted

Stock is counted for a line only when it is linked to a product: picked from your products on the invoice or bill, not just typed in.

- **Selling**: saving a Tax Invoice, Bill of Supply, Composition bill or Delivery Challan takes the quantity out. Change the quantity later and save, and only the difference moves.
- **Returns**: a Credit Note puts the quantity back.
- **Quotations and proformas** move no stock. The invoice you convert them into does.
- **Buying**: saving a [purchase bill](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#stock) adds the quantity in, and adds any new item to your products.
- **Cancelling** an invoice puts its stock back; un-cancelling takes it out again. Deleting an invoice puts its stock back too.
- **Making**: a production entry uses up raw materials and adds the finished product.

**Out of Stock** shows in red at zero or below. Purchases and deletions never take stock below zero; selling more than you have does, so you notice.

A service is never counted. Goods whose stock box was left blank are not counted either until stock first moves: a purchase bill adds to them from zero, and a sale takes them below zero, so you notice.

The [stock report](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#stock) shows each product's stock and value on any date.

### Correcting stock by hand

There is no separate stock adjustment screen. After counting your shelves, or for breakage, a free sample or opening stock:

- **One product**Click its pencil, type the real count in **Stock Quantity**, and click Update.
- **Many products**Click Bulk edit, type the counts in the **Stock** column, and click Save changes.

Stock typed in by hand has no date, so the stock report counts it as if it changed today. Write the reason in the product's description if you want to remember it.

Stock is one count per product. There are no batches, expiry dates, serial numbers or godowns. See [Limitations](https://billing.reazix.com/help/limitations.html#stock-limits).

## Low-stock alerts

A product at or below your threshold shows its stock in amber here, is listed on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#low-stock), and adds to the notification bell. The threshold is 5 to start; change it, or turn alerts off, in [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#stock). It is one threshold for every product. With alerts off, stock is still counted and **Out of Stock** still shows in red.

## Importing products from a spreadsheet

Have your price list in Excel, or moving from another program? Import (Excel / CSV) adds all the products and services at once.

- **Open the window**Click Import (Excel / CSV) on the Products screen. The window **Import products from Excel or CSV** opens.
- **Get the sample file**Click Download sample file. Products-sample.csv lands in your Downloads folder, with the right column headings and two demo rows: a product (Goods) and a service.
- **Fill it in**Open it in Excel or Google Sheets. Replace the two demo rows with your own, one product or service per row. Keep the first row (the headings) as it is.
- **Save it**Save it as Excel (.xlsx or .xls) or as CSV: all of them work.
- **Choose the file**Click Choose file (Excel or CSV). Nothing is saved yet: the window shows how many are ready, how many are already in your list (skipped), and every row with a problem.
- **Check**The window points out what to look at before importing: products at **0% GST** (choose the GST to give them, or keep 0% for exempt goods), stock **below zero** (tick to start it at 0), and products whose selling price was taken from the **MRP**.
- **Import**Click Import (it shows the number, such as **Import 40**). You see "Imported 40 products", and they appear in the list.

Moving from MARG, Tally, Busy or Vyapar
Export the item (stock) list from your old program to Excel and choose that file as it is: there is no need to fill in the sample file. A title or company name above the headings is passed over, a **Total** line at the end is left out, and the old program's headings are understood: Item Name, Item Code, HSNCode, P.Rate or Pur. Rate, Rate or Sale Rate, M.R.P., IGST (or SGST + CGST), Stock or Cl. Stock, UOM. Where the selling rate is 0 or blank, the MRP is used.

The columns (headings in small or capital letters, in any order; spaces, dots and % do not matter):

| Column heading | Holds |

| Name (or Product , Product Name , Item ) | Required. Rows without a name are skipped. |

| Type | Goods or Service . Blank means Goods. A service gets no stock. See Goods or service . |

| HSN/SAC (or HSN , SAC , HSN Code ) | HSN or SAC code |

| Unit | Nos if left out. Write it as in the app's list (Kg, Ltr, Pcs, Hrs, Page), so the GST returns get the right unit code. |

| Purchase Price (or Cost ) | What you pay for one unit |

| Selling Price (or Rate , Price ) | What you charge for one unit |

| GST % (or GST Rate , Tax % ) | GST rate, such as 18. 0 to 100. |

| Stock (or Quantity , Opening Stock ) | Opening stock of goods. Leave it blank for a service, or for goods you do not count. |

| Description | Optional |

The sample file looks like this:

```
Name,Type,HSN/SAC,Unit,Purchase Price,Selling Price,GST %,Stock,Description
Demo A4 Paper Ream 75 GSM,Goods,4802,Nos,220,280,18,50,Sample goods row - replace with your own
Demo Printing service,Service,998912,Page,,5,18,,Sample service row - a service has no stock
```

Products you already have (same name, any capitals) are skipped, and so are repeats inside the file, so importing the same file twice is safe. The CSV saved by the CSV button above the list uses the same columns, so you can export, edit in Excel and import into another copy of the app.

**Old invoices** are imported somewhere else: on the Dashboard, with CSV import / export, which has its own template. See [Importing and exporting invoices as CSV](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#csv). The link at the bottom of the import window goes there too.

**Something wrong?**A row is listed as a problem, such as "Row 4 (Tea): GST % must be 0 to 100" or "Type must be Goods or Service": fix that row in the file and choose it again (the rows already imported are skipped). Nothing is read: the file is not a plain CSV, or the headings are not in the first row. An .xlsx file renamed to .csv does not work. See [A CSV import did not work](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#csv-import).

## Manufacturing: making products from raw materials

If you make what you sell (furniture, sweets, garments, printed boxes), the app can use up the raw materials and add the finished product to stock in one step, and tell you what each unit costs you to make.

Turn it on first: [Settings → Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features), tick Manufacturing (bill of materials) and save. It is off to start, and turning it off again hides it without deleting anything. Once on, you get:

- a **Made here (from raw materials)** tick in the product form, for its bill of materials;
- a Make button at the top of Products, to record production;
- a Production list under the product table.

### 1. Give the product its raw materials (bill of materials)

A **bill of materials** is the recipe: which raw materials, and how much of each, go into **one** unit of the finished product.

- **Add the raw materials**Add each raw material as a normal product, with its purchase price and stock (or buy it in on a purchase bill).
- **Open the finished product**Click its pencil (or Add Product for a new one).
- **Tick Made here**Tick Made here (from raw materials). A box opens: **Raw materials used to make 1 unit of this product**.
- **List the materials**On each line, choose the material under **Choose a product…** and type the quantity for one unit made; its unit shows beside the box. Add material adds a line; the cross removes one.
- **Check the cost****Cost per unit** shows the materials' purchase prices times those quantities.
- **Save**Click Update (or Save). The list now shows **Made here · cost** under the name.

Rules, checked when you save: at least one material; a product chosen on every line; every quantity more than 0; no product listed twice (add the quantities together on one line); a product cannot be in its own list; and two products cannot use each other (chair uses seat, seat uses chair). The message says which, and nothing is saved.

A raw material can itself be made here (a seat made from wood and foam). If it has no purchase price, its cost comes from its own raw materials.

Unticking **Made here** and saving stops the product being made; production already recorded stays.

### 2. Make: record what you made

Each time a batch is finished, record it so stock stays right.

- **Open Make**Click Make at the top of Products. The window is **Make (record production)**.
- **Product made**Choose the product. Only products with a raw materials list are offered.
- **Quantity made**How many you made, in the product's unit.
- **Date**Today to start. Change it if you are recording a batch made earlier.
- **Note (optional)**Anything to remember, such as "Batch 12".
- **Check the table**Each raw material shows **Per unit**, **Will use**, **In stock** and **Left after**; the last row is the finished product with its stock after. Below it, **Cost of materials** for this batch, at today's purchase prices.
- **Save**Click Save production. You see "Production saved: 10 Nos of Chair", the stock changes, and the entry is added to the Production list.

If a raw material would go below zero, it is shown in red with a warning, and saving asks **Not enough raw materials in stock**; Save anyway goes ahead. That is fine when you record production late and have not entered the purchase bill yet.

**Something wrong?****No product has a raw materials list yet.**: give a product its raw materials first.
"Quantity made must be more than 0" or "Enter the date it was made": fill in those boxes. A message naming a product and a raw material means its list has a problem; open that product and fix the list.
"Could not save production, nothing was changed.": try again; if it keeps happening, see [Saving and working in the app](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving).

### Worked example

Reazix makes chairs. One chair takes 4 chair legs (₹50 each), 1 seat (₹300) and 0.2 kg screws (₹400 a kg), so the cost per unit is 4 × 50 + 300 + 0.2 × 400 = **₹580**. Stock before: 100 legs, 20 seats, 5 kg screws, 3 chairs.

| Make 10 chairs | Used | Stock after |

| Chair leg | 40 | 60 |

| Seat | 10 | 10 |

| Screws | 2 kg | 3 kg |

| Chair (made) | +10 | 13 |

The entry's cost of materials is 10 × ₹580 = ₹5,800.

### 3. The production list

Under the product table, **Production** lists the entries of the business you have open, newest first: **Date**, **Product**, **Qty made**, **Cost of materials** and **Note**.

| Control | What it does |

| From / To | Show only entries between these dates. Leave blank for all. |

| Print / PDF , Excel , CSV | Save the entries shown. |

| Eye (**View**) | Opens the entry: see below . |

| Bin (**Delete**) | Deletes the entry after asking, and puts its stock back exactly: in the example, 40 legs, 10 seats and 2 kg screws back, 10 chairs out. |

An entry cannot be edited: to change one, delete it and enter it again. The [stock report](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#stock) counts production by its date.

### Viewing a production entry

The eye opens **Made 10 Nos of Chair** (the quantity and product), with its date and note, and a table of each **Raw material used** with its **Qty**, **Rate** and **Cost**, and the **Total cost of materials**. The rates are the purchase prices on the day it was saved, so changing a price later does not change old entries. Delete deletes it as above; Close closes it.

---

# Payment receipts

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/receipts.html

Receipts for money you have received, whether against an invoice or not, ready to print.

A payment receipt is the slip you give a customer when they pay you: "Received ₹5,000 from Sharma Traders by UPI against invoice INV/2026-27/0012". Open Receipts in the sidebar to make, print, change or delete them. Each business keeps its own receipts: switching the business at the top of the sidebar shows that business's receipts only.

## The Payment Receipts list

The **Payment Receipts** card lists every receipt of the business you are working in, newest date first. Receipts you make here and the ones made when you record a payment on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments) both appear in it.

| Column | What it shows |

| **Date** | The date on the receipt. |

| **Receipt No** | Its number, such as RCP/2026-27/0012 (made here) or RCPT-... (made from a Dashboard payment). See Receipt numbers . |

| **Client** | Who paid you (**Received From**). |

| **Against Invoice** | The invoice it was for, or a dash if none. |

| **Amount** | The money received. |

| **Mode** | Bank Transfer, UPI, Cash, Cheque, Card or Other. |

| **Actions** | The printer prints it ( Printing ), the pencil edits it ( Editing ), the bin deletes it ( Deleting ). |

**Searching.** Type in the **Search receipts...** box above the list. It finds receipts whose client name or receipt number contains what you typed. Clear the box to see them all again.

**Empty list.** With no receipts yet you see "No receipts generated yet." and a Create Receipt button. With a search that finds nothing you see "No receipts match your search."

**Something wrong?**A receipt you made is missing: check the business selected at the top of the sidebar, since each business sees only its own receipts. A receipt from a Dashboard payment is missing: it is made when you click Record Payment, so a payment recorded in a very old version may not have one; print it from the invoice's Payment History instead.

## Receipts not assigned to a business

Receipts saved before the app kept businesses separate do not say which business took the money, so they show under every business. If you have any, a blue strip above the list says, for example, "**3 receipts** are not assigned to a business, so they show under all of them", with a button Assign to followed by the business you are working in.

Click it only if those receipts belong to that business. The app asks you to confirm, naming the business, and then they show only under it. The app never does this by itself, because only you know which business received the money. See [More than one business](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#multiple-businesses).

## Making a receipt (New Payment Receipt)

Make a receipt whenever a customer pays you and wants a slip, or when you want a record of money received: a payment against an invoice, an advance before you have billed, a security deposit, or any other money in.

**Paid against an invoice on the Dashboard?**If you record the payment on the invoice itself (the ₹ Payment button on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments)), a receipt is made for you. You do not need to make another one here.

- **Open the form**Click New Receipt at the top right. A box titled **New Payment Receipt** opens, with the next receipt number and today's date filled in.
- **Pick the invoice, if there is one**Under **Quick Select — Unpaid Invoices**, click the invoice being paid. The client, the amount still owed and the invoice number are filled in for you (more).
- **Check the amount**If the customer paid only part, change **Amount** to what they actually paid.
- **Choose how they paid**Pick the **Payment Mode** and type the UPI transaction ID, cheque number or bank reference in **Reference / Transaction No**.
- **Save**Click Save Receipt. You see "Receipt saved" and it appears in the list. Click the printer on its row to print it.

The fields in the form:

| Field | What to enter |

| **Receipt No** | Filled in with the next number. Leave it, and the number is confirmed when you save. Type your own if you need to (for example to match a paper receipt book), and yours is kept. See Receipt numbers . |

| **Date** | Today to start. Change it if the money came on another day. |

| **Received From (Client Name) *** | Required. Who paid you. Filled in when you pick an invoice. |

| **Amount *** | Required, more than 0. The money received, in rupees. |

| **Payment Mode** | Bank Transfer (the default), UPI, Cash, Cheque, Card or Other. Receipts in **Cash** also show in the [Cash book](https://billing.reazix.com/help/cash-book.html#from-elsewhere). |

| **Reference / Transaction No** | Optional. UPI reference, cheque number, NEFT/IMPS UTR and so on. It prints on the receipt. |

| **Against Invoice** | Optional. The invoice number this money is for, typed exactly as on the invoice, for example INV/2026-27/0012. Leave it empty for an advance or other money. See below . |

| **Note (optional)** | Anything else, such as "Advance for March order". It prints on the receipt. |

Cancel, or a click outside the box, closes it without saving. Anything typed is lost, so save first.

### Quick Select — Unpaid Invoices

This list at the top of the form shows up to 50 sales invoices of this business that are not fully paid: tax invoices, bills of supply and composition bills. Quotations, proforma invoices, delivery challans, credit notes and cancelled invoices are left out, because no money is owed on them. Each line shows the client, the invoice number and, on the right, the amount still owed. The list scrolls if it is long.

Clicking an invoice fills in **Received From**, the client's address (it prints on the receipt), **Amount** with what is still owed (less any TDS the client deducts, and never below zero) and **Against Invoice**. Once **Against Invoice** has something in it, the list hides. Empty that field to see the list again and pick a different invoice.

The list does not show when every invoice is paid, or when you have no sales invoices yet. Then just type the details.

### Against Invoice: what happens to the invoice

When **Against Invoice** exactly matches the number of one of this business's invoices, saving the receipt also records the payment on that invoice, with the same amount, date and mode and the note "Receipt RCP/... · ref ...". The invoice's status on the Dashboard then becomes **Partial** or **Paid**, and you do not record the payment again there. A cancelled invoice stays Cancelled.

If the number does not match any invoice (a typing mistake, or an invoice of another business), the receipt is still saved, and you see: "No invoice numbered ... was found, so this receipt is saved on its own." Nothing changes on any invoice. Check the number and edit the receipt if it was meant for an invoice.

For an **advance** (money before you have made the invoice), leave **Against Invoice** empty. The receipt stands on its own and no invoice changes.

**Something wrong?**"Client name required" or "Enter valid amount": fill in **Received From** and an **Amount** more than 0. The invoice did not become Paid: the number in **Against Invoice** must match exactly, including slashes and the year (picking from Quick Select avoids typing it), and the amount must cover what is owed. "Failed to save": the app could not reach its data; see [Saving and working in the app](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving).

## Editing a receipt (Edit Payment Receipt)

Click the pencil on a receipt's row. The same form opens, titled **Edit Payment Receipt**, with everything filled in. Change what you need and click Save Receipt. The receipt keeps its number.

- Changing the **Amount**, **Date** or **Payment Mode** of a receipt against an invoice updates the same payment on that invoice. It is not added twice.
- Changing **Against Invoice** to another invoice moves the payment: it is taken off the old invoice and recorded on the new one. Emptying it takes the payment off the old invoice.
- The receipt stays with the business it was made for, even if another business is selected while you edit it.

A receipt made from a Dashboard payment can be edited here too. You can also edit that payment on the Dashboard (Payment History, pencil), and its receipt follows.

## Receipt numbers

Receipts made on this screen have their own series, starting RCP, and follow your [invoice number format](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#invoice-numbers): separator, financial year (April to March) and digits, for example RCP/2026-27/0001. If you set a brand prefix, it is used for receipts too (ACME-RCP/...). A business with its own numbering numbers its receipts separately. Receipts never share a count with invoices.

The number you see when the form opens is a preview. The number is only taken when you save, so two people saving at once never get the same one. If you typed your own number, yours is kept and the series does not move.

Receipts made by recording a payment on the Dashboard are numbered differently, RCPT- followed by letters and numbers from the payment (for example RCPT-LX3K9A2B1C). That is normal.

## Printing a receipt

Click the printer on a receipt's row. The receipt opens in a new window and your browser's print box appears. Choose your printer, or **Save as PDF** to keep or send it on WhatsApp or email. The window closes after printing.

The printed receipt shows:

- Your business name, address and GSTIN (from [Company details](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details) of the business selected now), and the heading **PAYMENT RECEIPT**;
- **Receipt No**, **Date**, **Received From**, the client's **Address** (when the receipt was made from Quick Select), **Payment Mode**, and **Reference No** and **Against Invoice** when filled in;
- the amount in large figures, and in words underneath, then the note;
- signature lines for **Received By** and **Authorized Signatory**.

A payment recorded on the Dashboard also has a fuller receipt with the invoice total and balance, printed on A5 from the invoice's Payment History. See [The payment receipt](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#receipt).

**Something wrong?**"Your browser blocked the print window": allow pop-ups for the app in your browser (the icon at the right of the address bar) and click the printer again. See [Print does nothing](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked). It says "Your Business": fill in your business name in Settings, Company details.

## Deleting a receipt

Click the bin on the receipt's row. The app asks "Delete this receipt?"; click Delete to remove it. This cannot be undone.

Deleting a receipt removes only the receipt. A payment it recorded on an invoice stays on the invoice, so the invoice stays Paid or Partial. If the payment itself was a mistake, delete it from the invoice's Payment History on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments); that also removes its receipt.

## Cash receipts and the cash book

A receipt with Payment Mode **Cash** shows in the [Cash book](https://billing.reazix.com/help/cash-book.html#from-elsewhere) as money in, labelled with its receipt number, so you never type it there again. A receipt against an invoice and the payment it records on that invoice are the same money, and the cash book counts it once. To change it, change the receipt here; the cash book follows.

---

# Cash book

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/cash-book.html

Every rupee that comes in or goes out in cash, with names and notes, and how much cash you should have in the drawer right now.

## What the cash book is for

Use it for cash that does not belong on an invoice or a bill: money taken at the counter, an advance from a customer, salary paid in cash, tea and snacks, auto fare, money you take home, or cash you deposit in the bank. Each entry is either **Money in** or **Money out**, with an amount, a date, a name (who or what) and a note if you like.

Open it from Cash book in the sidebar. If you do not see it, tick **Cash book** under **Menu** in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features) and save. It is on to start, whatever your business type.

Each business has its own cash book, like its expenses and receipts. Switching the business at the top of the sidebar shows that business's cash.

The screen has, from top to bottom: the cash in hand cards, the entry form, the dates and search bar, and the list with its Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons.

## Start with the cash you have today

Count the cash in your drawer (or cash box) on the day you start, then add it as your first entry:

- **Money in**Make sure Money in is selected (it turns green).
- **Amount**Type the cash you counted, such as 12500.
- **Category**Click the Category box and pick **Opening balance**.
- **Save**Press Enter or click Save.

From then on, **Cash in hand** is this amount plus everything that comes in, less everything that goes out. While the cash book is empty, the list reminds you: "No cash entries yet. Add your cash in hand today as Money in, category Opening balance, to start."

## Adding an entry

The **New entry** form is at the top of the screen, so you can add one entry after another without opening anything.

- **In or out**Click Money in (green) for cash you received, or Money out (red) for cash you paid.
- **Amount**Required. More than 0, in rupees and paise.
- **Name**Who paid you or whom you paid, or what it was for: "Ramesh", "Milk", "Auto". Your clients' names, and names you used before, appear as you type.
- **Category**Optional. Pick one of Opening balance, Sales, Advance, Salary, Tea & snacks, Transport, Owner drawing, Deposit to bank or Other, or type your own.
- **Date**Today to start. Change it for an entry you forgot yesterday.
- **Note**Optional, anything you want to remember.
- **Save**Press Enter in any box, or click Save.

| Field | Details |

| **In or out *** | Money in or Money out . The one chosen is coloured. |

| **Amount *** | More than 0. Paise allowed (12.50). |

| **Name (who / what)** | Up to 120 letters. Suggestions come from your clients and names used before in this cash book. |

| **Category** | Pick from the list or type your own, up to 60 letters. Your own word is kept as you typed it. |

| **Date *** | The day the cash moved. |

| **Note** | Up to 500 letters. |

After saving you see, for example, "Money in of ₹500.00 saved". The entry appears in the list, and the amount, name, category and note are cleared for the next one. Money in or out and the date stay as they were, so ten counter sales in a row are quick.

**Something wrong?**If something is missing you see a message saying what to fix, and nothing is saved: "Enter an amount more than 0", "Enter a date", "Choose Money in or Money out", or "The name is too long (120 letters at most)". "Could not save the entry. Try again.": the app could not reach its data; see [Saving and working in the app](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving). The entry saved but you do not see it: it may be outside the dates chosen below the form; pick **All dates**.

## Cash already recorded in the app

You do not type cash in twice. These show in the cash book on their own, with a small dashed label saying where they came from:

| Label | Where it was made | Shows when |

| Invoice INV-5 payment | A payment recorded on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments) | The payment mode is Cash (money in) |

| Invoice CN-2 payment | A refund recorded on a credit note | The payment mode is Cash (money out) |

| Receipt RCP/26-27/0012 | A [payment receipt](https://billing.reazix.com/help/receipts.html); the invoice number follows if it was against one | The payment mode is Cash (money in) |

| Expense | An [expense](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html#add-expense); its category shows too | The payment mode is Cash (money out) |

| Purchase bill GS/0457 payment | A [payment to a supplier](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#record-payment) recorded on a purchase bill, with the supplier's name and the reference | The payment mode is Cash (money out) |

These lines cannot be edited or deleted in the cash book (they have no pencil or bin). Click the label to go to the screen it was made on, and change it there; the cash book follows.

**Counted once.** Recording a payment on the Dashboard also makes a receipt, and a receipt against an invoice also records a payment on it. It is the same money, so the cash book shows it once, as the receipt.

**Paying suppliers.** Record a cash payment to a supplier on the purchase bill (green ₹ button in Purchases), not here: it then shows here once, and the bill's balance goes down too. A bill marked Paid from the Status dropdown is not counted as cash (how it was paid is not known). If you added supplier payments here by hand before, and now record them on the bill as well, delete your own entry. See [Cash payments and the Cash book](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#payments-cash-book).

Invoices and receipts in another currency (export invoices in dollars, for example) are left out: the cash book is in rupees.

## Cash in hand and the totals

The cards at the top show:

- **Cash in hand**: all money in, less all money out, up to today. Entries dated in the future are not counted until their day comes. It turns red if it goes below zero, which usually means an entry is missing or the opening balance was not added.
- **Today**: cash in and out today.
- **This month**: cash in and out since the 1st.

These cards always count every line, whatever dates or search you choose for the list.

Count the drawer at the end of the day and compare it with Cash in hand. If they differ, look for an entry you forgot.

**Something wrong?**Cash in hand is red or too low: add your opening balance, and check that cash sales recorded on invoices or receipts used mode **Cash**. It is too high: a cash payment may be entered here and also on a receipt; delete your own entry, since the receipt already counts.

## The list and the running balance

The list's title is the dates you chose (such as **This month**) with the money in and out of the lines shown. The list is oldest first, like a paper cash book; on the same day, lines go in the order entered, money in before money out. Each line shows the date, name and note, category (or where it came from), the amount under **Money in** or **Money out**, and the **Balance**: the cash you had after that line. A line with no name shows "Money in" or "Money out".

The first line, **Opening balance (brought forward)**, is the cash you had when the chosen dates begin. With **All dates** there is no such line. The last line, **Closing balance**, is the cash at the end of them, with the total in and out. When nothing falls in the dates, you see "Nothing in these dates."

### Changing or deleting an entry (Edit entry)

Your own entries have a pencil and a bin under **Actions**. The pencil opens the entry in the form at the top, now titled **Edit entry**. Change it and click Update, or Cancel to leave it as it was. After an update the form is ready for a new entry again, dated today.

The bin deletes the entry. The app asks first, saying how cash in hand will change ("Money out of ₹200.00 on 05 Oct 2026 (Auto) is removed from the cash book..."). Click Delete. This cannot be undone.

Lines from invoices, receipts and expenses have no pencil or bin. Change them where they were made (see above).

## Choosing dates and searching

The bar between the form and the list chooses which lines the list shows.

| Choice | Shows |

| **This month** | The 1st to the last day of this month. The choice when you open the screen. |

| **Last month** | The whole of last month. |

| **This financial year** | 1 April to 31 March of the current year. |

| **All dates** | Everything, from your first entry. |

| **Choose dates** | Two date boxes appear: a from date and a to date. Leave one empty for no limit on that side. |

The **Search name, note, category...** box finds lines by name, note, category, where they came from (such as a receipt or invoice number), or amount. While you search, the totals at the bottom add up only the lines found, and the last line reads **Total of these lines**; each line still shows its real balance. The red X button (it shows once you search or change the dates) clears the search and goes back to This month.

## Print, PDF and Excel

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV above the list save the lines shown, with the dates and search you chose: the opening balance, each line with its balance, and the total. The columns are Date, Name, Note, Category, From (where the line came from, or "Cash book" for your own entries), Money in, Money out and Balance. To make a PDF, click Print / PDF and choose **Save as PDF** as the printer. The CSV opens in Excel too.

Your cash book is also saved in your backups. In [Export Backup](https://billing.reazix.com/help/backup.html#export-import) it travels with **Expenses**.

**Something wrong?**"Nothing to export": no lines are shown for the dates and search chosen; widen the dates. Print / PDF does nothing: allow pop-ups for the app; see [Print does nothing](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked).

---

# Recurring invoices

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/recurring.html

Invoices that repeat on a schedule, such as a monthly retainer, rent or an annual maintenance contract.

A recurring invoice is a template: the client, the items and a schedule. On each due date the app makes a real invoice from it by itself, with a fresh number, ready for you to check and send.
