Use it for anything you bill the same way again and again: monthly rent, an accountant's retainer, an AMC (annual maintenance contract), a weekly supply.

## Two ways to set one up

- **From an invoice** (recommended): make the first invoice as usual, and under Customize tick [Make this a recurring invoice](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoice-options.html#recurring). This keeps everything on the invoice, including HSN/SAC codes, discounts, taxes, place of supply, terms and options, and lets you set **Every N** and an end date or number of invoices.
- **From the Recurring screen**: New Template with a client, frequency, next date, when to stop, type and simple item lines (below). Quicker, but the item lines have no HSN/SAC code or discount.

Both appear in the same Recurring Templates list and are made into invoices the same way.

## The New Recurring Invoice form

Click New Template at the top right (or Create Template when the list is empty). A box titled **New Recurring Invoice** opens.

- **Pick the client**Click them under **Quick Select Client** (why this matters), or type the **Client Name**.
- **Set the schedule**Choose the **Frequency** and **Every**, and the **Next Due Date**: the date of the first invoice.
- **Say when to stop**Leave **Stop** at Never, or pick a date or a number of invoices.
- **Add the items**Fill in at least one line under Line Items.
- **Save**Click Save. You see "Recurring invoice created" and it appears in the list.

| Field | What it does |

| **Quick Select Client** | Your saved clients. Picking one fills in the name and GSTIN, and also keeps their state, address, country and SEZ status for the invoices. |

| **Client Name *** | Required. Printed on every invoice. |

| **Client GSTIN** | Optional, 15 characters. Leave empty for a customer without GST (B2C). |

| **Frequency** | Weekly, Monthly (the default), Quarterly or Yearly. |

| **Every** | 1 to 12. 1 means every period. Monthly with 3 means every three months; Weekly with 2 means every fortnight. |

| **Next Due Date** | When the next invoice is made. The 1st of next month, to start. Monthly schedules come back to this day of the month: start on the 31st and you get 31 January, 28 (or 29) February, 31 March. |

| **Stop** | **Never (until I stop it)**; **On a specific date**, which shows **Stop after this date** (an invoice due on that date is still made); or **After N invoices**, which shows **Number of invoices**, such as 12 for a one-year monthly contract. |

| **Invoice Type** | Tax Invoice (the default), Quotation, Proforma / Estimate, Bill of Supply (No GST), Composition (Bill of Supply), Credit Note or Delivery Challan. Each type uses its own number series (INV, QUO, EST, BOS, COMP, CN, DC). |

| **Line Items** | What you bill each time. See Line Items . |

Cancel, or a click outside the box, closes it without saving.

### Quick Select Client

This list shows when you start a new template, you have saved [clients](https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html), and **Client Name** is still empty. Each line shows the client's name, state and GSTIN. Clicking one fills in the form and hides the list. To pick someone else, empty **Client Name** and the list comes back.

**Why pick rather than type:** the client's state, country and SEZ status decide the tax on each invoice: CGST + SGST for a client in your own state, IGST for another state, an SEZ or a client abroad. These are not shown in the form, so they are only kept when you pick the client from the list. A name typed by hand has no state saved with it. See [GST terms](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms) for place of supply, CGST, SGST and IGST.

### Line Items

Each line is one thing you bill every time:

| Field | What to enter |

| **Description** | What it is, such as "Monthly accounting retainer" or "Shop rent, Ground floor". A line with no description is left out when you save. |

| **Qty** | How many, 1 to start. |

| **Rate** | The price of one, before GST. |

| **GST%** | The GST rate, 18 to start. Use 0 for exempt items or a bill of supply. |

Add Item adds another line. The red X at the end of a line removes it (it shows once there is more than one line). You need at least one line with a description and a rate, or you see "Add at least one item with description and rate".

The amount in the list is worked out from these lines with the full GST rules, exactly as the invoice will be.

**Something wrong?**"Client name required": fill in **Client Name**. The invoices charge IGST instead of CGST + SGST, or the other way round: the client's state was not saved; delete the template and make it again, picking the client from Quick Select (or make it from an invoice). See [The invoice has the wrong tax split](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#wrong-tax) and [Set your business State](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#state-missing). You need an HSN/SAC code or a discount on the lines: make the template [from an invoice](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoice-options.html#recurring).

## The Recurring Templates list

Every template of the business you are working in, by client name A to Z.

| Column | What it shows |

| **Client** | Who is billed. |

| **Frequency** | Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly, or "Every 3 months" and so on. |

| **Type** | The invoice type made. |

| **Amount** | The total of each invoice, with GST, in the template's currency. |

| **Next Due** | When the next invoice will be made. Shown in bold orange, and the row is highlighted, when it is due today or overdue. |

| **Status** | **Active** (green) or **Paused** (grey). |

| **Actions** | ▶ Generate Now (green), Pause or Activate, the pencil to edit , the bin to delete . |

## Invoices due for generation

When an **Active** template's next date has come and its invoice has not been made yet, an orange box at the top says, for example, "**2 invoices due for generation**", with one button per template showing the client and frequency (such as "Sharma Traders — Monthly").

Usually you do nothing: the app makes them by itself within the hour (see below). Click a button to make that invoice straight away; it works exactly like Generate Now. Paused templates never show here.

## How invoices are created automatically

A few seconds after the app starts, and then every hour while it is running, every **Active** template whose next date has come, and which has not reached its end, creates its invoice:

- a fresh number in that type's series (and the business's own series, if it has one);
- that day's date, status Unpaid, and a due date the same number of days later as on the invoice it was made from (none for templates made on this screen);
- the client, items and full GST working: CGST + SGST or IGST, cess, TDS/TCS, discounts and round-off, as on the invoice screen.

Its **Next Due** then moves on by the schedule, and it stops at its end condition. The notification bell says how many were made today ("2 recurring invoices auto-generated today"). They appear on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#invoice-list), ready to check and send.

If the app was closed for a while, a missed month is not skipped: one invoice is made at start-up and one more at each hourly check, until the template has caught up. Each is dated the day it is made; change the date on the invoice if you need the missed date.

**Something wrong?**No invoice was made: check that the template is **Active**, its **Next Due** is today or earlier, it has not reached its **Stop** condition, and the app is running. Two invoices for one month: the template was caught up after the app was closed, or ▶ was clicked as well; delete or cancel the extra one on the Dashboard. "Invoice number ... already exists": see [this fix](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#duplicate-number).

## Generate Now

▶ creates the invoice straight away, even if the template is paused or not yet due, exactly as the automatic run would: same tax, a fresh number, today's date. You see "Invoice INV/2026-27/0042 generated for ..." Its next date moves on by the schedule and it counts towards "After N invoices". Once a template has reached its end, you see "Failed to generate: This template has reached its end date or number of invoices" instead. Open the new invoice from the Dashboard to check it before sending.

## Editing a template (Edit Template)

Click the pencil on a template's row. The form opens titled **Edit Template**, with everything filled in. Change the schedule, stop condition, type or lines and click Update. You see "Template updated". Invoices already made do not change; the next one uses the new details.

- Everything the form does not show is kept: terms, notes, invoice options, HSN codes and discounts on the lines, tax-inclusive prices, place of supply, and the client's state and country.
- Changing **Next Due Date** also moves the day of the month the schedule comes back to.
- Quick Select Client does not show while editing. To bill a different client, make a new template.
- Saving files the template under the business selected now, so edit it while that business is selected.

## Pause, Activate and Delete

**Pause** (the pause button on an Active row) stops the automatic invoices but keeps the template; you see "Paused". The button becomes **Activate** (a play button); click it to start again ("Activated"). If the next date passed while it was paused, the invoice is made at the next check. Use Pause for a client who stops for a few months.

**Delete** (the bin) asks "Delete this recurring invoice?"; click Delete template. No more invoices are made from it. Invoices already made stay on the Dashboard. This cannot be undone.

## Templates not assigned to a business

Templates saved before the app kept businesses separate show under every business. If you have any, a blue strip says, for example, "**2 recurring templates** are not assigned to a business", with a button Assign to followed by the business selected now. Click it only if they belong to that business; the app asks you to confirm first. See [More than one business](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#multiple-businesses).

---

# Purchase bills

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html

Record every supplier bill, so the GST you paid comes back as input tax credit and your stock stays right. Includes reading a bill from a photo, importing bills from a CSV file, and purchase orders to send suppliers.

**Purchase bill or expense?**
Use **Purchases** for goods you buy to sell or to make things with (stock), from a supplier's tax invoice. Use [Expenses](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html) for running costs that are not stock: rent, electricity, phone, software, travel, salary. Enter each bill in one place only. A bill entered in both is counted twice, and its GST is claimed twice in GSTR-3B.

## The purchase list

Open **Purchases** from the menu. The screen is called **Purchase Bills**, or **Purchases** when purchase orders are turned on. Then two buttons sit under the title: Purchase bills (the list on this page) and Purchase orders.

The buttons at the top right:

| Button | What it does |

| Import from image (OCR) | Reads a photo of a supplier's bill and fills the form for you. See Reading a bill from a photo . |

| CSV import / export | Brings in many bills at once from a spreadsheet, or saves all of them as one CSV. See Importing purchase bills from CSV . |

| Add Purchase | Opens a blank purchase bill. See Adding a purchase bill . |

### The four totals

**Total Purchases** is the full value of the bills shown, with GST, cess and round-off. **Owed to suppliers** is what you still have to pay on those bills (see What you owe suppliers). **GST (ITC Eligible)** is the GST on those bills (CGST + SGST + IGST, without cess): the input tax credit they give you. **Entries** is how many bills are shown. All four follow the search and filters below them, so picking last year shows last year's totals.

### Search and filters

- **Search supplier, invoice...**: type part of a supplier's name, their invoice number or their GSTIN.
- **Year**: the current financial year (April to March) to start. Pick one of the last five years, or **All years**.
- **All bills** / **Unpaid / Partly paid** / **Paid**: pick **Unpaid / Partly paid** to see only the bills you still have to pay.
- **Cost centre**: only when [cost centres](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#cost-centres) are turned on. **All cost centres**, **No cost centre**, or one branch, site or project.
- The red ✕ clears the search, the status and the cost centre. The year stays as it is.

### Purchase Records

The table lists **Date**, **Supplier**, **GSTIN**, **Invoice No**, **Taxable** (value before GST), **Tax** (GST), **Total**, **Balance due** (what is still to pay, in red; a dash when nothing is), **Status** and **Actions**, newest first, with a **Total** row at the bottom. The Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons at the top of the table save the purchase register.

| On each row | What it does |

| **Status** dropdown | Unpaid, Partly paid or Paid. Picking Paid or Unpaid saves at once; Partly paid opens the payment window for the amount. See Marking a bill paid from the list . |

| Eye | Opens the bill to look at, without downloading anything. See Viewing a bill . |

| ₹ (green) | Records a payment to the supplier, and shows the payments already made. See Recording a payment to a supplier . |

| Pencil | Opens the bill in the form to change it. |

| Bin | Deletes the bill, after asking. Its quantities are taken back out of stock (see What saving does to your products ). GST credit already claimed in a return you filed stays as filed. |

With no bills yet, the table says **No purchase bills recorded yet.** with an Add Purchase button. If you have bills but the filters hide them all, it says **No purchases match your filters.**: clear the search or pick **All years**.

**Something wrong?**
**A bill I entered is missing.** Check the year: a bill dated March 2026 is in FY 2025-26, not the current year. Pick **All years** and search for the invoice number. Also check the business selected in the sidebar: each business sees only its own bills.

**The same bills show under two businesses.** They were saved before you kept businesses separate. See Not assigned to a business.

### Viewing a bill

Click the eye on a row. A window titled **Purchase Bill · **invoice number shows:

- the date, payment status, and **Intrastate (CGST+SGST)** or **Interstate (IGST)**;
- the **Supplier** box: name, address and GSTIN;
- the items: **#**, **Description**, **HSN**, **Qty**, **Rate**, **GST%** and **Amount** (quantity × rate, plus GST);
- the totals: **Taxable**, then **CGST** and **SGST** (half each) or **IGST**, **Cess** and **Round-off** when there are any, and the **TOTAL**;
- **Less: TDS** and **Paid to supplier** when you keep back TDS, then **Paid** (the payments added up) and **Balance due**;
- **Payments made**: each payment's date, amount, mode and reference;
- the note, if the bill has one.

| Button | What it does |

| Close | Closes the window. Clicking outside it does the same. |

| Payments | Opens the payment window to record, change or delete a payment. See Recording a payment to a supplier . |

| Edit | Opens the bill in the form. |

| Download PDF | Saves a one-page A4 **PURCHASE BILL** PDF named Purchase- invoice no - date .pdf , with the supplier, the items, the tax split and the total, then the payments made, **Paid** and **Balance due**. Long item names wrap onto more lines instead of being cut. The coloured lines follow your PDF accent colour in [print settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/print-settings.html#colours). |

This PDF is your own record of the bill. It is not a tax invoice: the supplier's bill is.

## Adding a purchase bill

Click Add Purchase. The **Add Purchase Bill** form opens (**Edit Purchase Bill** when you clicked a pencil). Copy the details from the supplier's bill.

| Field | What to put in |

| **Date *** | The date on the supplier's bill. Today to start. This decides which month's GSTR-3B the credit goes into. |

| **Payment Status** | Unpaid (to start) or Paid. Paid records one payment for the whole amount. To record what you actually paid (a part payment, UPI, cash), save the bill and use the green ₹ button in the list. Once a bill has payments, this box only shows its status. See Paying suppliers . |

| **Supplier Name *** | Required. Suppliers from your earlier bills are suggested as you type. Picking one fills in their GSTIN, address and **Inter-state purchase** from their last bill. |

| **Supplier GSTIN** | The supplier's 15-character GST number, from the top of their bill. Typing the full GSTIN ticks or unticks **Inter-state purchase** for you (see Suppliers in another state ). Leave it blank for an unregistered supplier. |

| **Supplier Address (optional)** | Street, city, state. Printed on the purchase bill PDF. |

| **Invoice Number *** | Required. The supplier's invoice number exactly as printed, such as GS/2026/0457 . GSTR-2B matching uses it, so do not shorten it. |

| **Note (optional)** | Anything for yourself, such as "paid by cheque 004512". |

| **Cost centre** | Only when cost centres are on. The branch, site or project this bill belongs to, or **None**. See [Cost centres](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#cost-centres). |

| **Inter-state purchase** | Tick when the supplier charged IGST. See Suppliers in another state . |

Under the fields come the Items, the running totals and Apply round-off.

- **Supplier**Type the supplier's name. If you have bought from them before, pick them from the list: GSTIN and address fill in.
- **Bill details**Set the **Date** and type the **Invoice Number** from their bill. Leave **Payment Status** on Unpaid and record the payment after saving (see how), or pick Paid if you paid it all and do not need the details.
- **Items**Add one row for each line on their bill: name, HSN, quantity, rate before GST, and GST rate. See Items on the bill.
- **Check the total**The strip under the items shows Taxable, CGST and SGST (or IGST), Cess and Total. Compare them with the supplier's bill. If only the paise differ, tick **Apply round-off**.
- **Save**Click Save (Update when editing). Cancel, or clicking outside the form, closes it without saving.

After saving, the message **Purchase added — items synced to Products** appears, the bill is at the top of the list, and the quantities are added to your product stock.

A bill made from a purchase order shows **From purchase order** PO number under the title. See Turning a purchase order into a bill.

**Something wrong?**
**"Supplier name is required"** or **"Invoice number is required"**: fill in that field. **"Add at least one item with a quantity and rate"**: a bill needs at least one item with a name, a quantity and a rate above zero.

**My total does not match the supplier's bill.** Check that **Rate** is the price before GST (the taxable rate), that each **Tax %** is right, and that cess is entered. Then check **Inter-state purchase**: it changes the split, not the total. Paise differences are what round-off is for.

**The wrong GSTIN came in when I picked a supplier.** The suggestion uses their last bill. Type the correct GSTIN over it; it is kept.

**"Failed to save purchase"**: the app could not reach its data. See [Saving problems](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving).

### TDS on a purchase bill

If you must deduct income-tax TDS when you pay this supplier (a contractor under 194C, a professional under 194J, rent under 194I...), record it on the bill. Under the totals strip, tick **TDS deducted**:

- **Section**Pick the section. Its usual rate fills in.
- **Rate or amount**Check the **Rate %**: the TDS is worked out on the taxable value (before GST), and the amount box shows it as a hint. To use an exact figure instead, type it in the amount box.
- **Check**The strip shows **Less TDS** and **Paid to supplier** (the bill total less the TDS): that is what you pay the supplier. The bill's total itself does not change, and nor does the GST credit.

When you record payments on this bill, they are measured against **Paid to supplier**, not the total: paying that amount makes the bill **Paid**, and its **Balance due** is what is left of it.

The view and the PDF of the bill show the TDS and **Paid to supplier** under the total. Every bill with TDS is listed in [Reports, TDS & TCS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#tds-on-purchases), totalled by section and quarter, for depositing the TDS and filing your Form 26Q. You need a TAN to deduct TDS; ask your CA whether a payment needs it.

### Items on the bill

Each row of **Items** is one line of the supplier's bill.

| Column | What to put in |

| **Name** | The item. As you type, your products and items from earlier bills are suggested (your Products list first). Picking one fills in its **HSN**, its purchase price as **Rate**, its **Tax %** and **Cess %**. Use the same name as in Products, so stock goes to the right product. |

| **HSN** | The HSN code (goods) or SAC code (services) printed on the supplier's bill. |

| **Qty** | How many. Decimals are fine: 2.5 kg, 0.75 m. |

| **Rate** | The price of **one** unit **before GST**, as on the supplier's bill. |

| **Tax %** | The GST rate: 0%, 0.1%, 0.25%, 3%, 5%, 12%, 18% (to start), 28% or 40%. For any other rate pick Other… : a box asks for a rate between 0 and 100 (up to two decimals), then Apply rate . |

| **Cess %** | Compensation cess, only for goods that carry it (tobacco, pan masala, aerated drinks, coal, some vehicles). 0 for everything else. |

| Bin | Removes the row. The last row cannot be removed. |

Add Item adds a new row and puts the cursor in its name, so you can keep typing: Tab to the button, Enter, and type the next item.

Clicking **Qty**, **Rate** or **Cess %** selects what is in it, so typing replaces it (you get 18, not 018).

If you pick a different item in the same row, its details replace the old item's. A value you typed yourself is kept.

The strip under the items adds up as you type: **Taxable** (quantity × rate for every row), **CGST** and **SGST** (half the GST each) or **IGST** for an inter-state bill, **Cess** when there is any, **Round-off** when ticked, and **Total**.

**HSN, CGST, SGST, IGST?**
**HSN** is the code for the type of goods (**SAC** for services). **CGST** and **SGST** are the central and state halves of GST, charged when the supplier is in your state; **IGST** is the single tax charged when they are in another state. See the [glossary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms).

## Round-off

Most suppliers round their bill total to the nearest rupee. If yours did, tick **Apply round-off** under the items, so your total matches theirs: ₹1,234.56 becomes ₹1,235 (round-off +₹0.44), ₹1,234.40 becomes ₹1,234 (round-off −₹0.40).

It is off to start, because many bills already match the items exactly. The round-off is kept separate: it changes the bill's total, not its GST, so your input tax credit stays exactly what the supplier charged. It shows on the view, the PDF and the purchase register.

An old bill with a round-off amount saved on it opens with the box already ticked.

## Suppliers in another state

When a supplier is in **your** state, their bill charges **CGST + SGST**. When they are in a **different** state, it charges **IGST** instead. Tick **Inter-state purchase** for an IGST bill, so the credit goes to IGST in GSTR-3B rather than CGST and SGST. Getting it wrong puts the credit in the wrong column.

You rarely need to tick it yourself:

- **Typing the supplier's full GSTIN** ticks or unticks it. The first two digits of a GSTIN are the state code (03 Punjab, 07 Delhi, 27 Maharashtra...), compared with the state of your business in [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details).
- **Picking a supplier** you have bought from before uses what their last bill had.
- **Reading a bill photo** ticks it when the bill shows IGST and no CGST.

You can still change it by hand, for the rare exception. Simply look at the supplier's bill: IGST printed means ticked; CGST and SGST printed means not ticked.

**Something wrong?**
If the box does not tick itself when you type a GSTIN, your own state may be missing. Fill in **State** in [Settings, Company Details](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details). See also [The wrong tax split](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#wrong-tax).

## How the GST credit is used

Input tax credit (ITC) is the GST you paid on what you bought, which you subtract from the GST you collected on sales. The app adds up the GST on every purchase bill and every [expense](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html#gst-credit) in the period, and puts it in Table 4 (Eligible ITC) of [GSTR-3B](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#gstr-3b): to IGST for an inter-state bill, otherwise half to CGST and half to SGST. Cess on purchase bills goes in as cess credit. The credit goes into the month of the bill's **Date**.

The purchase form has no switch for reverse charge, blocked credit or a separate place of supply. Every bill's GST is counted as credit. So:

- **Check against GSTR-2B.** Only credit your supplier has reported usually can be claimed. Import your GSTR-2B on the GST Returns screen and compare: see [Checking your credit against GSTR-2B](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#gstr-2b). Matching uses the supplier GSTIN and invoice number, so type them exactly.
- **Credit you cannot claim** (food and drinks, personal use, motor cars in most cases, a supplier who has not filed): leave it out when you file on the portal, or ask your CA. The app does not know which credit is blocked.
- **Reverse charge** (you pay the GST instead of the supplier, for example on goods transport or legal services): the app does not work this out on purchases. Ask your CA how to show it.

Purchase bills also feed the [Income Tax](https://billing.reazix.com/help/income-tax.html#itr-summary) screen (your purchases, without GST, are subtracted from sales). The [Profit & Loss](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#profit-loss) report on Reports uses sales and expenses only, not purchase bills.

## Paying suppliers

Each time you pay a supplier, record the payment on their bill: how much, when, and how (cash, UPI, bank transfer, cheque, card). You can pay a bill in parts, and record as many payments as you made. The app then shows what each bill, and each supplier, still needs to be paid.

Each bill has a status, shown in colour in the **Status** column of the list:

| Status | Means |

| **Unpaid** (amber) | No payment recorded yet. The whole amount is still to pay. |

| **Partly paid** (purple) | Some payments are recorded, but they add up to less than the bill. **Balance due** shows what is left. |

| **Paid** (green) | The payments add up to the bill (less any TDS you keep back). Nothing is due. |

You do not set the status by hand: it follows the payments. Record a payment and it changes; delete one and it changes back.

The status does not change the GST credit: credit depends on the bill, not on whether you have paid it yet. (By law you must pay the supplier within 180 days to keep the credit.)

**Bills from before payments could be recorded**
A bill you marked **Paid** in an older version has no payments on it. It stays **Paid** and owes nothing; you do not need to do anything. A bill marked **Partial** stays Partly paid, but the app does not know how much was paid, so its Balance due shows the whole amount until you record the payments you made.

### Recording a payment to a supplier

In **Purchase Records**, find the bill and click the green ₹ button under **Actions** (or open the bill with the eye and click Payments). The window **Record payment to supplier** opens. At the top it shows the bill number and supplier, the **Total**, **Less TDS** if you keep back TDS, what is **Paid** so far and the **Balance** still to pay.

- **Amount paid**It starts at the balance still to pay. Leave it to pay the bill off, or type what you actually paid, such as 5000.
- **Payment date**Today to start. Change it to the day the money left you.
- **Payment mode**Cash, UPI, Bank transfer, Cheque, Card or Other.
- **Reference / cheque no.**Optional: the UTR or UPI reference from your bank, or the cheque number.
- **Note**Optional, anything you want to remember.
- **Save**Click Record Payment. The message says how much was recorded and what is left, for example "Payment of ₹5,000.00 recorded · ₹6,800.00 left to pay".

| Field | Details |

| **Amount paid *** | More than 0, paise allowed. It cannot be more than the balance still to pay (a rupee over is allowed for rounding). |

| **Payment date *** | The day you paid. |

| **Payment mode** | Bank transfer to start. Pick **Cash** for cash: it then shows in the Cash book too. |

| **Reference / cheque no.** | Up to 60 letters. |

| **Note (optional)** | Up to 300 letters. |

After saving, the list shows the new **Balance due** and status straight away.

**Something wrong?**
**"That is more than the ₹... still to pay on this bill"**: the amount is more than the balance. Check the amount, or the payments already recorded (they are listed under **Payment History** in the same window). If you really paid the supplier more, the extra is an advance against their next bill: record only the bill's balance here and note the rest.

**"Enter an amount more than 0"** or **"Enter the payment date"**: fill in that box.

**"Could not save the payment. Try again."**: the app could not reach its data. See [Saving problems](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving).

### Part payments

Pay a bill in as many parts as you like. Each part is one payment. For example, a bill of ₹11,800:

- **First part**Click ₹, type 5000, pick **UPI**, add the UPI reference and click Record Payment. The bill is now **Partly paid** and its Balance due is ₹6,800.
- **The rest**Later, click ₹ again. The amount already says 6800. Pick **Cash** and click Record Payment. The bill is now **Paid**, and the ₹6,800 shows in the Cash book as money out.

Payments made to a supplier in one go for several bills: record one payment on each bill, for the part of the money that went to it.

### Payment history: changing or deleting a payment

Every payment on a bill is listed under **Payment History** in the payment window, oldest first: date, amount, mode, and the reference and note. The status of the bill is under the list. The same payments show in the bill's view (eye) and on its PDF, under **Payments made**.

- **Change a payment**: click its pencil. The boxes above fill with that payment and the title becomes **Edit payment**. Change what you need and click Save payment, or Cancel edit to leave it as it was.
- **Delete a payment**: click its red bin. The app asks first, saying the amount and date. Click Delete payment. The bill goes back to Partly paid or Unpaid, and a cash payment leaves the Cash book.

### Marking a bill paid from the list

The **Status** dropdown on each row is a shortcut:

- **Paid** records one payment for the whole balance, dated today, mode **Other** and noted "Marked paid", and says **Marked paid**. Use it when you do not need the details. Mode Other is not counted as cash, so it does not show in the Cash book.
- **Unpaid** takes back that "Marked paid" payment. Payments you recorded yourself stay: the bill then stays Partly paid and the message says so; delete them from the ₹ window if they were wrong.
- **Partly paid** opens the payment window, because a part payment needs its amount.

Choosing **Paid** in the bill form does the same as choosing it here.

### What you owe suppliers

Four places show what is still to pay:

- The **Owed to suppliers** card above the list: the balance due on all the bills shown (it follows the year, search and filters; pick **All years** for everything).
- The **Balance due** column, with its total at the bottom. Pick **Unpaid / Partly paid** in the filters to see only those bills.
- The purchase register (Print / PDF, Excel, CSV), which has **Paid** and **Balance due** columns. See For your accountant.
- [Reports, Party Outstanding](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#supplier-outstanding) with **You owe suppliers**: one row per supplier, month by month, like Tally.

The balance of a bill is its total, less TDS you keep back, less the payments recorded. A bill marked Paid before payments could be recorded owes nothing.

### Cash payments and the Cash book

A payment with mode **Cash** shows in the [Cash book](https://billing.reazix.com/help/cash-book.html#from-elsewhere) by itself, as money out, labelled **Purchase bill** number **payment**, with the supplier's name and the reference. It is counted once. Do not also add it in the Cash book.

To change or delete it, click its label in the Cash book (it opens Purchases), then use the ₹ button on the bill. The Cash book follows.

If you added supplier cash payments to the Cash book by hand before this version, and now also record them on the bill, delete your own Cash book entry so the money is not counted twice.

UPI, bank transfer, cheque, card and Other payments are not cash, so they do not show in the Cash book.

## What saving does to your products

Each item on the bill is matched to your [products](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html) by name (capitals do not matter):

- **A product you already have**: its stock goes up by the quantity, and its purchase price becomes this bill's rate. Its selling price is not touched. Its HSN, GST rate and cess are filled in from the bill only if the product had none.
- **A new item**: it is added to your products, with the rate as both purchase and selling price, unit **Nos** (or the unit from the purchase order), and the quantity as its stock. **Check its selling price afterwards** in Products, or you will sell at cost.
- **Editing a bill**: only the difference is added. Change 10 to 12 and stock goes up by 2; remove a row and its quantity is taken back out.
- **Deleting a bill**: its quantities are taken back out of stock.

Stock can go below zero (if you sold before you entered the purchase); it is not stopped at zero.

**Something wrong?**
**A second product appeared with a slightly different name** ("Pen drive 32GB" and "Pendrive 32 GB"). The bill's name did not match. Pick the item from the suggestions when typing a bill. To fix it, edit the bill to use the right name (the stock moves back), then delete the extra product.

**"Purchase saved, but updating stock in Products failed"**: the bill is saved; check the stock of its items in [Products](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html#stock) and correct it there.

## Reading a bill from a photo

Instead of typing a long bill, let the app read it from a photo or scan. Click Import from image (OCR). The window **Import from bill image (OCR)** opens.

- **Choose the picture**Click the dashed box, or drag a photo or scan of the bill onto it: PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 8 MB. PDFs are not accepted; take a screenshot of the page instead. A preview appears.
- **Read it**Click Extract fields. **Reading image…** shows a percentage. It takes a few seconds, longer on an older computer.
- **Check everything**The **Extracted fields** panel appears on the right. Correct anything it read wrong, and add or remove item rows. See Checking what was read.
- **Use it**Click Use these values. The **Add Purchase Bill** form opens with it all filled in.
- **Check once more and save**Compare the form's total with the bill, fix any rate or tax, and click Save.

Everything is read on your own computer, in English, with no internet needed and nothing uploaded anywhere.

**For best results:** a sharp, straight, well-lit photo of a printed bill, taken from above, with the whole bill in the frame and nothing else. Handwritten bills, crumpled paper, shadows and photos at an angle read badly.

**Something wrong?**
**"Please upload an image (PNG, JPG, WebP)."**: you chose a PDF or another file. **"Image is over 8MB"**: take a smaller photo, or crop it. **"OCR failed: ..."**: the message ends with a hint; see [Reading a bill photo failed](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#ocr-failed). If a bill will not read well, type it in with Add Purchase: suggestions make it quick for suppliers and items you have used before.

### Checking what was read

The **Extracted fields** panel shows what the app found. Every box can be changed.

| Field | What to check |

| **Supplier** | Read from the capital-letter line above their GSTIN. Often needs correcting. |

| **GSTIN** | The first GSTIN on the bill. If the bill shows your GSTIN before the supplier's, replace it with theirs. |

| **Invoice No.** | The number after "Invoice", "Bill" or "No.". |

| **Date** | Read day first, as on Indian bills (03/04/2026 is 3 April). |

| **Grand total** | The amount after "Grand Total", "Amount Payable", "Total" or "Net Amount". Used only when no item rows are found. |

**Tax breakdown**, when found, lists the Taxable value, CGST, SGST / UTGST, IGST, Cess and Round-off printed on the bill, for you to compare. They are not copied into the form: the form works its own figures out from the items.

**Line items** shows each row it read, with the number found in brackets. Each row has the name, **HSN/SAC**, **Qty**, **Rate ₹**, **GST%** and **Amount ₹**, and a bin to remove it. Add row adds an empty one. A row that matches one of your saved products shows **Matched saved product:** name (with a percentage of how close the names are), and takes that product's GST rate and, if the bill had none, its HSN.

Check each row against the bill. The commonest mistakes: the **Rate** is really the line amount, the quantity was missed (it then shows 1), or a total line was read as an item. The **Amount** is only for comparing; the form uses quantity × rate.

**Raw OCR text** (click to open) shows everything the app read, if you want to copy a figure from it.

Use these values shows how many rows will go into the form. In the form, items come in with cess 0, so add cess yourself if the bill has it. A row where no GST % was found comes in at 0%: set its real **Tax %**. If no rows were found but a total was, one row named **From OCR — split into real items** holds the total: replace it with the real items and their GST rates before saving. **Inter-state purchase** is ticked when the bill showed IGST and no CGST.

## For your accountant

The Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons at the top of **Purchase Records** save the **Purchase register**: the bills shown, after the search, year, status and cost centre filters, oldest first, with a **Total** row. Your business name is at the top.

Columns: **Date**, **Supplier**, **GSTIN**, **Invoice No**, **Taxable Amount**, **CGST**, **SGST**, **IGST**, **Cess**, **Inter-state** (Y or N), **Round-off**, **Total**, **Paid** (payments to the supplier), **Balance due**, **Status** and **Note**.

- Print / PDF opens the register on its own page in landscape. Choose your printer, or **Save as PDF**. If nothing opens, allow pop-ups for the app (the message **"Allow pop-ups for this page to print the report"** appears).
- Excel downloads an .xlsx file, with numbers as numbers.
- CSV downloads the same as a CSV file.

For one quarter, pick the year and give your CA the file; they can filter the dates. The register has one row per bill. To get one row per item (and a file you can import back), use Export all as CSV in CSV import / export.

## Importing purchase bills from CSV

Use this to bring in many bills at once: from another billing program, from Tally, or a sheet your accountant keeps. Click CSV import / export at the top of Purchases. The window **Purchase bills: CSV import / export** opens.

| Button | What it does |

| Template | Downloads Purchase-import-template.csv : the right columns and one example bill. |

| Export all as CSV | Downloads every purchase bill of this business as Purchase-bills- date .csv , one row per item, in the same columns. Good for a backup, or to move bills to another business. |

| Choose CSV file | Reads your file and shows what will happen. Nothing is saved yet. |

| Import | Saves the bills that are ready. The button shows how many. |

| Close | Closes without importing. |

- **Start from the template**Click Template. Open it in Excel or Google Sheets, delete the example row, and fill in your bills. Save it as **CSV** (in Excel: **File → Save As → CSV (Comma delimited)**).
- **Choose the file**Click Choose CSV file. A box shows the file name, how many bills are **ready**, how many are **already there (skipped)**, and every problem, row by row (a bad date, a missing rate, no item name).
- **Fix problems**Bills with problems are not imported. Fix them in the file, save it, and choose it again.
- **Import**Click Import. A message says how many were imported, how many skipped, and how many had errors.

### The columns

One row per item. Rows with the same supplier and invoice number make one bill.

| Column | What to know |

| **Invoice Number** | Required. The supplier's bill number. |

| **Invoice Date** | Required. YYYY-MM-DD (2026-10-03) or DD-MM-YYYY (03-10-2026). |

| **Supplier Name**, **Supplier GSTIN** | At least one of the two. A bill with only a GSTIN uses it as the name. |

| **Supplier Address** | Optional. |

| **Item Name** | Required on every row. |

| **HSN/SAC** | Optional. |

| **Quantity** | 1 if blank. |

| **Rate** | Required. Per unit, before GST. |

| **GST %**, **Cess %** | 0 if blank. GST up to 100. |

| **Inter-state** | Yes or No. If blank, it is worked out from the supplier's GSTIN and your state. |

| **Payment Status** | Unpaid, Partial or Paid. Unpaid if blank. |

| **Note** | Optional. |

Other common headings are understood too: **Bill No**, **Vendor**, **Party Name**, **GSTIN**, **Item**, **Particulars**, **HSN**, **Qty**, **Price**, **Tax %**, **Remarks** and so on, so a file from another program often works as it is.

A bill already entered (same supplier and invoice number, matched by GSTIN or by name) is skipped, never changed. Imported bills have no round-off. Quantities are added to product stock and new items become products, as when you type a bill in (see What saving does to your products).

**Something wrong?**
**"The dates are month first"**: your Excel wrote dates as MM/DD/YYYY. Change the date column to DD-MM-YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD. A yellow line saying **Dates are read day first** is a reminder to check one example date.

**"The file has no rows under the header"**, or nothing is read: the file is not a real CSV, or the headings are not in the first row. See [A CSV import did not work](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#csv-import).

**A bill was skipped that I wanted.** One with the same supplier and invoice number is already there. Delete it first if you want to bring it in again.

## Purchase orders

A purchase order (PO) is what you send a supplier **before** the goods come: what you want, how many, at what rate. It is not a bill, so it changes neither your stock nor your GST returns. When the goods come, you turn it into a purchase bill in one click.

Turn it on in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features): tick **Purchase orders** under **Purchases screen**, and save. It is on to start if you picked **Wholesale / trading** or **Manufacturing** as your [business type](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#business-type). Purchases then has two buttons under the title, Purchase bills and Purchase orders. On the purchase orders tab, the top-right button is New purchase order.

- **Make one**Click New purchase order, fill in the supplier and items, and Save. See The purchase order form.
- **Send it**Click the eye to view it, then WhatsApp, Email, Print or Download PDF. See Viewing and sending a purchase order.
- **When the goods come**Click Convert to purchase bill, type the supplier's bill number, change any quantity to what actually came, and Save. See Turning a purchase order into a bill.

### The purchase order list

Search by PO number, supplier or GSTIN in **Search PO number, supplier...**, and filter by status with **All statuses**. The red ✕ clears both.

The **Purchase orders** table lists **PO number**, **Date**, **Supplier**, **Expected** (delivery date), **Total** (with GST) and **Status**. The actions on each row:

| Button | What it does | Shown for |

| Eye | View the order | Every order |

| Pencil | Edit the order | Open orders only |

| Green page | Convert to purchase bill | Open and Partly received |

| ⋯ menu | Duplicate , Print , Download PDF , WhatsApp , Email , Cancel order | Received and Cancelled orders show only Duplicate |

With no orders yet, the list says **No purchase orders yet.** with a New purchase order button.

### Purchase order status

The status is worked out from the purchase bills made from the order; you only set Cancelled yourself.

| Status | Means |

| Open | No bill saved from it yet. You can edit it. |

| Partly received | Bills saved from it have less than was ordered. Convert to purchase bill again fills in only what is still to come. |

| Received | Bills saved from it cover every item. |

| Cancelled | You cancelled it with Cancel order in the row's ⋯ menu. It keeps its number. |

Received and cancelled orders can only be viewed and duplicated (Duplicate starts a new PO with the same supplier, items and notes, and a new number). Items are matched between the order and its bills by name, so keep the item names the same on the bill.

**Cancelling:** Cancel order asks first. Cancel order again confirms, Keep it leaves it. Bills already saved from it stay as they are. A cancelled order cannot be made Open again; duplicate it instead.

### The purchase order form

New purchase order opens **New purchase order** (**Edit purchase order** from the pencil). It is the purchase bill form with a few changes:

| Field | What to put in |

| **PO date *** | The date of the order. Today to start. |

| **Expected delivery** | Optional. When you want the goods. Printed on the PO as **Expected by**. |

| **Supplier Name ***, **Supplier GSTIN** | As on a bill. Suppliers from your purchase bills are suggested. |

| **Supplier Address (optional)** | Printed on the PO. |

| **PO number *** | Filled in for you as PO/26-27/0001 , counting up for each business and financial year. You can type your own. |

| **Notes / terms (optional)** | Delivery address, payment terms, packing. Printed on the PO under **Notes / terms**. |

| **Cost centre** | Only when cost centres are on. A bill made from the PO gets the same one. |

| **Inter-state purchase** | Tick for a supplier in another state: the PO shows IGST instead of CGST + SGST. |

The **Items** are the same as on a bill (see Items on the bill) with one more column, **Unit** (Nos, Kg, Box...), filled in from the product. There is no Payment Status and no round-off. Rows without a name or a quantity are left out when you save.

A number is never handed out twice. If you type a number already used by another PO, the message **"... is already used by another purchase order"** appears; change it.

**Something wrong?**
**"PO date is required"**, **"Supplier name is required"**, **"Add at least one item with a quantity"**: fill those in. **"Could not get the next PO number. Type one in PO number."**: the app could not reach its data for a moment; type a number yourself, or close and try again.

### Viewing and sending a purchase order

The eye opens **Purchase order · **PO number: the date, expected date, status and tax type, the supplier, the items with **Unit**, **Taxable value**, CGST and SGST or IGST, cess, **TOTAL** and your **Notes / terms**.

| Button | What it does |

| Close | Closes the window. |

| Duplicate | A new PO with the same supplier and items. |

| Edit | Open orders only. |

| WhatsApp | On a phone that can share files, sends the PDF with a short message. On a computer, opens WhatsApp with the message (PO number, date, items, quantities, rates and total) for you to pick the supplier; attach the PDF yourself if you want it. |

| Email | Opens your email program with the subject **Purchase order** number and the order typed out. Add the supplier's email address, and attach the PDF from Download PDF if you want. |

| Print | Opens the PDF ready to print. If pop-ups are blocked, it downloads instead. |

| Download PDF | Saves the PDF, named after the PO number with _ for each slash, such as PO_26-27_0001.pdf . |

| Convert to purchase bill | See Turning a purchase order into a bill . |

Received and cancelled orders show only Close and Duplicate.

The PDF is an A4 **PURCHASE ORDER**: your business name, address, state, GSTIN, phone and email at the top; the PO number, date and expected date; **TO (SUPPLIER)**; the items; taxable value, CGST and SGST (or IGST), cess and **TOTAL (INR)** with the amount in words; your notes; and **For** your business with your signature image (from your business details or [print settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/print-settings.html#signature)) and **Authorised signatory**.

### Turning a purchase order into a bill

- **Click Convert**Click the green Convert to purchase bill on the row, or the same button in the view.
- **The bill form opens**The **Add Purchase Bill** form shows **From purchase order** PO number, with the supplier, the items still to come, their rates, GST and cost centre filled in. The date is today.
- **Type the supplier's bill number**In **Invoice Number**, from the bill that came with the goods. Set the **Date** to the date on their bill.
- **Change quantities**If fewer came, change **Qty** to what actually came. Change a rate if the bill differs.
- **Save**The bill is saved, stock goes up, and the order becomes Partly received or Received.

When the rest comes, convert the same order again: only what is still to come is filled in. Deleting a bill made from an order takes the stock back out and puts the order back to Open or Partly received.

## "Not assigned to a business"

This only matters if you keep [more than one business](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#multiple-businesses) in the app. Records saved before you began keeping businesses separate have no business recorded, so they show under **every** business. Nothing is hidden, so nothing goes missing.

When there are any, a blue banner says, for example, **3 purchase bills are not assigned to a business, so they show under all of them.** The same banner appears on [Expenses](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html), [Recurring](https://billing.reazix.com/help/recurring.html) and [Receipts](https://billing.reazix.com/help/receipts.html), for their own records.

- **Pick the right business**Switch to the business those records belong to in the sidebar.
- **Assign**Click Assign to business name on the banner. A box asks you to confirm, naming the business.
- **Confirm**Click Assign to business name again. The records now belong to that business only, and no longer show under the others. The banner goes away.

**Only if they all belong to it**
The button assigns **all** the unassigned records on that screen to the business selected. The app never guesses. If some belong to one business and some to another, do not use the button: open each one under the right business instead, or ask on the [support page](https://billing.reazix.com/help/support.html).

**Something wrong?**
**"Could not assign — please try again"**: the app could not save for a moment; click again. If it keeps happening, see [Saving problems](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#saving).

---

# Expenses

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html

Costs that are not stock, such as rent, electricity, software or travel, for your profit and loss, your income tax and the GST credit on them.

**Expense or purchase bill?**
Goods you buy to sell, with a supplier's tax invoice, go in [Purchases](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html) (they add to stock). Everything else you spend to run the business goes here. Enter each bill in one place only, or it is counted, and its GST claimed, twice.

## The expense list

Open **Expenses** from the menu. Add Expense at the top right opens a new expense.

### The three totals

**Total Expenses** is everything you paid, with GST. **GST Paid (ITC)** is the GST inside those amounts, your input tax credit. **Entries** is how many expenses are shown. All three follow the search and filters.

### Search and filters

- **Search expenses...**: part of the description, the vendor's name or the bill number.
- **All Categories**: show one category only, such as Office Rent.
- **Year**: the current financial year (April to March) to start; one of the last five, or **All years**.
- **Cost centre**: only when [cost centres](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#cost-centres) are on.
- The red ✕ clears the search, category and cost centre, and puts the year back to the current one.

### Expense Records

The table lists **Date**, **Description**, **Category**, **Vendor**, **Amount**, **GST** and **Mode** (how you paid), with a **Total** row. The pencil opens an expense to change it; the bin deletes it, after asking. The Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons save the expense statement.

With nothing yet, it says **No expenses recorded yet.**; with filters hiding everything, **No expenses match your filters.**

**Something wrong?**
**An expense is missing.** Check the year (an expense dated in March belongs to the year that ends that March), the category filter, and the business selected in the sidebar. If old expenses show under every business, see [Not assigned to a business](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#unassigned).

## Adding an expense

Click Add Expense. The **Add Expense** form opens (**Edit Expense** from the pencil).

| Field | What to put in |

| **Date *** | The date on the bill, or the day you paid. Today to start. It decides the month the GST credit goes into. |

| **Category** | What kind of cost it is. **Other** to start. See Categories . |

| **Description *** | Required. What it was for, such as "Shop rent - October" or "AWS Hosting - March". |

| **Amount (incl. GST) *** | Required, above zero. The full amount you paid, with GST. |

| **GST % (for ITC)** | The GST rate on the bill, such as 18. The GST inside the amount is worked out and shown underneath as **GST: ₹...**. Leave it blank (or 0) when the bill has no GST: rent from an unregistered owner, salary, bank charges without GST. |

| **Vendor Name** | Who you paid. Optional, but needed to claim the credit. |

| **Vendor GSTIN** | Their 15-character GSTIN, from their bill. Needed to claim the credit. |

| **Invoice / Bill No** | Their bill number. Optional. |

| **Payment Mode** | Bank Transfer (to start), UPI, Cash, Cheque, Card or Other. Expenses paid in **Cash** appear in the [Cash book](https://billing.reazix.com/help/cash-book.html#from-elsewhere) as money out. |

| **Cost centre** | Only when cost centres are on. The branch, site or project it belongs to. |

| **Inter-state expense** | Tick when the vendor charged IGST (a different state), as with cloud and software firms billing from another state. The first two digits of their GSTIN are their state code. |

| **Note (optional)** | Anything for yourself. |

- **Pick the category**And type a **Description** you will recognise later.
- **Type the amount**The total on the bill, with GST.
- **Type the GST rate**If the bill shows GST. Check the **GST: ₹...** underneath against the GST printed on the bill.
- **Vendor details**Name, GSTIN and bill number, if you will claim the credit.
- **Save**Click Save (Update when editing). The message **Expense added** appears.

**Example:** internet bill ₹1,180 with 18% GST. Amount 1180, GST % 18: the app shows GST ₹180 (1180 × 18 ÷ 118), and the cost without GST is ₹1,000.

**Something wrong?**
**"Description is required"** or **"Enter a valid amount"**: fill in a description and an amount above zero. **"GST % must be between 0 and 100"**: type just the number, such as 18.

**The GST shown differs a little from the bill**: the bill may be rounded. It is worked out from the amount and rate; if the difference matters, check the amount you typed is the bill's total with GST, not before.

**Deleting an expense** removes it from your list, reports and future returns. Credit already claimed in a return you filed stays as filed.

## Categories

Office Rent, Utilities, Internet & Phone, Software & Tools, Travel, Meals & Entertainment, Office Supplies, Salary & Wages, Professional Fees, Insurance, Marketing & Ads, Raw Materials, Shipping & Courier, Repairs & Maintenance, Bank Charges, GST Paid, Asset Purchase, Personal / Drawings, and Other. The list is fixed; use **Other** with a clear description for anything else.

| Category | Use it for |

| Asset Purchase | Things that last years: a computer, furniture, a machine, a vehicle. The [Income Tax](https://billing.reazix.com/help/income-tax.html) screen leaves these out of business expenses (assets are written off over years as depreciation, not in one go). |

| Personal / Drawings | Money you take out for yourself or spend on the family from the business account. Left out of business expenses on the Income Tax screen. |

| Salary & Wages | Pay to staff. Usually no GST. |

| Raw Materials | Small material buys without a proper tax invoice. Material bought on a supplier's GST bill, which you want in stock, belongs in [Purchases](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html). |

| GST Paid | Only for cases your CA tells you to record this way. The GST you pay the government on your returns is not an expense. |

The [Profit & Loss](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#profit-loss) report includes every category, without GST. Use the category filter on the list to see, for example, all Office Rent for the year.

## How the GST credit is used

The GST on each expense is added to your input tax credit in Table 4 of [GSTR-3B](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#gstr-3b), in the month of its date: to IGST if **Inter-state expense** is ticked, otherwise half to CGST and half to SGST. It is added to the credit from your [purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#itc).

Every expense with a GST % is counted. Only claim credit you are entitled to:

- The vendor must be GST-registered, and their bill must show your GSTIN. Without the vendor's GSTIN, put the GST % as 0.
- Food and drinks, personal spending, club fees and most car costs usually do not qualify (blocked credit). Put the GST % as 0 for these.
- Check the total against your GSTR-2B: see [Checking your credit against GSTR-2B](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#gstr-2b).

In the [Profit & Loss](https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html#profit-loss) report, the GST on expenses is taken off, so your costs are shown without the GST you get back.

## For your accountant

The Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons at the top of **Expense Records** save the **Expense statement**: the rows shown, oldest first, with a **Total** row. The heading names your business and what was chosen (the year, the category, the cost centre, the search), and so does the file name: for example Expenses-FY 2026-27, Office Rent.

Columns: **Date**, **Description**, **Category**, **Amount**, **GST Amount**, **GST %**, **Vendor**, **Vendor GSTIN**, **Invoice No**, **Payment Mode**, **Inter-state** (Y or N) and **Note**.

- **Choose what to include**Pick the year, and a category or cost centre, or search. For example: all Rent for the year.
- **Save it**Excel downloads an .xlsx file, CSV a CSV file, and Print / PDF opens it on its own page to print or **Save as PDF**.

**Something wrong?**
**Print / PDF does nothing**, or says **"Allow pop-ups for this page to print the report"**: allow pop-ups for the app in your browser and click again. See [Print does nothing](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked).

---

# GST returns

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html

GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B built from the invoices, purchases and expenses you have already entered, checked against GSTR-2B, and ready to upload to the GST portal.

**The app prepares, you file**
The app works out the figures and makes the files. It does not log in to the GST portal. Filing is always done by you, or your CA, on gst.gov.in. Open the screen from **GST Returns** in the sidebar.

## GST words on this screen, in plain language

You do not need to be an accountant to use this screen. These are the words it uses. The [glossary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms) has more.

| Word | What it means for you |

| **GSTR-1** | The return that lists your sales : who you billed, how much, and the GST on it. Filed every month (by the 11th) or every quarter under QRMP (by the 13th after the quarter). |

| **GSTR-3B** | The short summary return where you pay the tax: GST collected on sales, less the GST you paid on purchases. Filed by the 20th (monthly) or the 22nd/24th after the quarter (QRMP), depending on your state. |

| **GSTR-2B** | A statement the portal makes for you every month, listing the purchase invoices your suppliers have reported. It shows which purchase GST you can claim back. |

| **B2B** | Business to business: a sale to a client who has a GSTIN. Reported invoice by invoice, because your client claims credit for that GST. |

| **B2C** | Business to consumer: a sale to someone with no GSTIN (a walk-in customer, a person, an unregistered shop). Mostly reported as totals, not invoice by invoice. |

| **B2C Large (B2CL)** | An inter-state B2C invoice above ₹1 lakh (₹2.5 lakh for invoices dated before 1 August 2024). These are reported one by one. |

| **GSTIN** | The 15-character GST number, such as 27ABCDE1234F1Z5. The first two digits are the state code (27 is Maharashtra). |

| **CGST, SGST, IGST** | Inside your own state, GST is split half Central (CGST) and half State (SGST, or UTGST in a Union Territory). To another state, it is one Integrated tax (IGST). The app decides this from your state and the place of supply. |

| **Place of supply (POS)** | The state the sale is treated as made in, usually the buyer's state. It decides CGST + SGST or IGST, and which state gets the tax. Shown as a code, such as 10 for Bihar. |

| **Intra-state / Inter-state** | Intra: you and the place of supply are in the same state (CGST + SGST). Inter: different states (IGST). |

| **ITC (input tax credit)** | The GST you paid on purchases and business expenses. You subtract it from the GST you collected, and pay only the difference. |

| **HSN / SAC code** | The official code for what you sell: HSN for goods, SAC (starts with 99) for services. GSTR-1 needs a summary by code. |

| **Credit note / debit note** | A credit note reduces an invoice you already issued (goods returned, a discount after the sale). It lowers your tax. A debit note increases one. The app makes credit notes. |

| **Reverse charge (RCM)** | A few supplies where the buyer pays the GST instead of the seller, such as goods transport (GTA) or legal services. |

| **Zero-rated** | Exports and sales to SEZ units. Taxed at 0%, or IGST paid and later refunded. |

| **QRMP** | Quarterly Return, Monthly Payment: small businesses (up to ₹5 crore turnover) can file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B every quarter. |

| **NIL return** | A return for a period with nothing to report. It is still compulsory. |

## Choosing the period

The row at the top, next to **GST Returns**, chooses the period every tab shows. It opens on the current month.

| Control | What it does |

| First list: **Monthly**, **Quarterly (QRMP)** or **Full Year** | How long the period is. Pick Monthly if you file every month, Quarterly (QRMP) if you file every quarter. |

| Month and year (Monthly) | January to December, and a year from this year back five years. |

| Quarter and year (Quarterly) | Q1 (Apr–Jun), Q2 (Jul–Sep), Q3 (Oct–Dec) or Q4 (Jan–Mar). The year is the calendar year of those months, so the Jan–Mar 2027 quarter is **Q4** with **2027**, and Apr–Jun 2026 is **Q1** with **2026**. |

| Financial year (Full Year) | A financial year, such as FY 2026-27 (April to March). Useful for checking a whole year, or for your CA. |

| **R1 Pending / R1 Filed** and **3B Pending / 3B Filed** | Whether you have filed GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for this period. Click to switch. See Filed status . |

| GST Portal | Opens gst.gov.in in your browser. |

An invoice, purchase or expense belongs to the period of its **date**. Everything shown is for the business selected at the top of the sidebar only: each GSTIN files its own returns.

The files the app makes carry the **return period** the portal expects: the month for a monthly return, the last month of the quarter for a quarterly one (Q1 2026 is 062026), and March of the closing year for a full year.

**Something wrong?**
Figures look empty or too small? Check the period type (Monthly or Quarterly) and the year first: Jan–Mar is Q4 with the new calendar year. Then check the business in the sidebar. See ["No data to export for this period"](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#nothing-to-export).

## What is included

- **Tax tables (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B)** use **tax invoices** and **credit notes** only.
- **Left out of the tax tables**: proforma estimates, quotations, bills of supply, composition bills, delivery challans, and cancelled invoices.
- **Document Summary (Table 13)** also counts bills of supply, composition bills, delivery challans, and cancelled documents, as the portal asks. See Document Summary.
- **B2B or B2C** is decided by the client: a client with a GSTIN is B2B, one without is B2C.
- **Exports** (a client whose country is not India) are kept out of B2B and B2C and listed in the red box. See Exports and SEZ.
- **Input tax credit** comes from your [purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html) and [expenses with GST](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html#gst-credit) dated in the period.
- **Only the selected business**: invoices, purchases and expenses of other businesses you keep in the app are never mixed in.

**Composition, annual and other returns**
This screen prepares GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for a regular GST business. It does not make CMP-08, GSTR-4 (composition), GSTR-9 (annual) or TDS/TCS forms. The figures here, and the CSV files, help your CA prepare those.

## Filed status, warnings and the summary strip

Above the tabs you see, from top to bottom: the period row, a red box and an amber box if anything needs fixing, a NIL banner if the period is empty, and a strip of four totals. Below them are the tabs:

| Tab | What it is for |

| **GSTR-1** | Your sales, in the portal's tables, with the JSON file to upload. See GSTR-1 . |

| **GSTR-3B** | Tax on sales, credit on purchases, and what you pay. See GSTR-3B . |

| **GSTR-2B Reconciliation** | Checks your purchase bills against GSTR-2B. Shown only while **GSTR-2B matching** is on in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features) (it is on to start). See GSTR-2B . |

| **TDS / TCS Report** | TDS your clients deducted and TCS you collected. See TDS and TCS . |

| **Filing Guide** | Step-by-step portal instructions. See Filing Guide . |

The small ? next to the tabs opens the guide for the tab you are on.

### Filed status (R1 and 3B)

The two small pills in the period row remember whether you have filed:

- **R1 Pending** (red) or **R1 Filed** (green): GSTR-1.
- **3B Pending** (red) or **3B Filed** (green): GSTR-3B.
- **File on the portal first**The app cannot see the portal, so it only knows what you tell it.
- **Mark it**Click the pill, or Mark Filed on the GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B tab. A message confirms "GSTR1 marked as filed for this period".
- **Undo a mistake**Click the green pill again: it goes back to Pending.

The mark is kept in this browser, for each business (GSTIN) and each period. Monthly, quarterly and full-year periods are separate: marking Q1 filed does not mark April, May and June. Another computer or browser does not see your marks.

### The red and amber warning boxes

The app checks the period's invoices and shows problems before you file. The **red box** is for problems that make the return wrong or that the portal rejects. The **amber box** is for things worth fixing. Each box shows the first three messages; fix them and the next ones appear (the amber box also says "+N more").

| Message | What to do |

| "**N export invoice(s) (…) are not in the GSTR-1 file.** Add them in Table 6A on the GST portal with the shipping bill details" | Nothing is wrong with the invoices. On the portal, enter each export in Table 6A with its shipping bill number, date and port code. See Exports . |

| "Invoice X: **Invalid client GSTIN format** — …" | The client's GSTIN is mistyped. Correct it on the [client](https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html#client-form) and on the invoice, then save the invoice again. |

| "Invoice X: **inter-state sale** to … **without the buyer's state as Place of Supply**" | A B2C sale charged IGST, but its place of supply is missing or is your own state. The portal refuses that. Open the invoice, set [Place of Supply](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#details) to the buyer's state, and save. |

| "**Your business GSTIN is not set.** Go to Settings → Company Details to add it." | Add it in [Settings, Company Details](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details). The files need it. |

| Amber: "Invoice X: Item "…" **has no HSN/SAC code**" | Add the code to the item on the invoice (and on the [product](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html#add-product), so future bills have it). Without it the item is left out of the HSN table in the JSON. |

| Amber: "Invoice X: Client … **has GSTIN but no State**" | Set the client's state, or the invoice's Place of Supply. Otherwise the place of supply may come out wrong. |

**Something wrong?**
Fixed an invoice but the message is still there? Save the invoice, then come back to GST Returns (switch to another screen and back) so it reads the invoices again. For a wrong CGST/IGST split, see [The invoice has the wrong tax split](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#wrong-tax).

### The summary strip

| Figure | What it counts |

| **Invoices** | Tax invoices and credit notes in the period, exports included |

| **Taxable** | Taxable value of B2B and B2C sales, less credit notes (exports not included) |

| **Tax** | CGST + SGST + IGST on those sales, less credit notes |

| **Net Payable** | What is left to pay in cash after your input tax credit, as on the GSTR-3B tab |

## GSTR-1: your sales

The GSTR-1 tab lays your sales out in the same tables as the portal, so you can check them before you upload. At the top is a row of buttons (see GSTR-1 downloads). Below are these cards:

| Card | Portal table | What is in it |

| B2B Sales — Table 4A | 4A | Invoices to clients with a GSTIN, one row each |

| Credit/Debit Notes — Table 9B | 9B | Credit notes issued in the period (shown only if there are any) |

| B2C Sales — Table 7 | 7 and 5 | Sales to buyers without a GSTIN, added up; B2C Large invoices listed under them |

| HSN Summary — Table 12 | 12 | Quantity, value and tax for each HSN/SAC code |

| Document Summary — Table 13 | 13 | Number ranges of documents issued, and how many were cancelled |

| GSTR-1 Summary Totals | - | B2B and B2C together, less credit notes |

Exports to clients abroad are not in these tables or in the GSTR-1 file. The red box lists them: add them in Table 6A on the portal with the shipping bill details.

### B2B Sales — Table 4A

Every tax invoice to a client with a GSTIN, one row each. Your client sees these in their GSTR-2B and claims the GST as credit, so they must be right. The heading shows how many invoices there are.

| Column | Meaning |

| GSTIN | The client's GSTIN, from the invoice |

| Client, Invoice No, Date | As on the invoice |

| POS | Place of supply as a state code (27, 10, 07…) |

| Type | **Intra** (CGST + SGST) or **Inter** (IGST), exactly as the invoice charged it |

| Taxable, CGST, SGST, IGST | Taxable value and tax. UTGST (Union Territories) is shown under SGST, as the portal takes it. |

| Total | The invoice total |

The last row, **B2B Total**, adds them up. "No B2B invoices for this period." means no invoice in the period had a client GSTIN.

In the JSON, a [reverse-charge](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#reverse-charge) invoice is marked so, and an invoice to an SEZ client goes in as an SEZ supply (with or without payment of tax, from the invoice's LUT option).

**Something wrong?**
A sale to a business is in B2C instead? The client had no GSTIN on that invoice. Add the GSTIN to the client, open the invoice, pick the client again so the GSTIN is copied in, and save. Wrong Intra/Inter? See [wrong tax split](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#wrong-tax).

### Credit/Debit Notes — Table 9B

Shown only when the period has [credit notes](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#credit-note). One row per note: the client's GSTIN (or **Unregistered**), client, note number, date, taxable value, tax and total.

- Credit notes **reduce** your sales and tax. They are subtracted in the Summary Totals, the HSN Summary and GSTR-3B.
- Notes to clients with a GSTIN go in the JSON file (CDNR). Notes to **unregistered** buyers are **not** in the JSON: download them with CDNR (the file GSTR1_CDNUR.csv) and enter them on the portal under 9B (Unregistered), if the portal asks for them.
- The app does not make debit notes. If you issue one, add it on the portal by hand.

### B2C Sales — Table 7

Sales to buyers without a GSTIN. The portal does not want them one by one: it wants totals for each **supply type**, **place of supply** and **tax rate**, and that is how the card shows them.

| Column | Meaning |

| Type | **Intra-state**, **Inter-state**, or **Inter-state, large** for a B2C Large invoice |

| Place of supply | State code and name, such as 10-Bihar |

| Rate % | The GST rate. For a large invoice this column shows its invoice number instead. |

| Taxable, CGST, SGST, IGST, Total | Added up for that row |

**B2C Large (Table 5).** An inter-state invoice to an unregistered buyer above ₹1 lakh (₹2.5 lakh for invoices before 1 August 2024) is listed on its own row, marked **Inter-state, large**, and goes in the file invoice by invoice. The heading shows how many there are, such as "12 invoices (1 B2C Large)".

The last row, **B2C Total**, adds up all B2C sales. Credit notes are not taken off here; they are subtracted once, in the Summary Totals.

**Something wrong?**
An inter-state sale shows in the red box? Its place of supply is missing or is your own state. Open the invoice, set [Place of Supply](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#details) to the buyer's state, and save. A walk-in sale in your own state should be **Intra-state**: if it is not, check your state in [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details).

### HSN Summary — Table 12

One row for each HSN/SAC code, tax rate and unit, covering B2B, B2C, exports and credit notes together. The portal requires this table.

| Column | Meaning |

| HSN | The code on the item. **N/A** means the item had none. |

| Description | The name of the first item with that code |

| Qty | Total quantity. Credit notes subtract. |

| Taxable, CGST, SGST, IGST, Total Tax | Added up, net of credit notes |

How many digits you need depends on your turnover: 4 digits up to ₹5 crore, 6 digits above. Tick **Aggregate turnover (AATO) is above ₹5 crore** in [Settings, GSTR filing details](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#gstr-details) if that is you, and the app checks for 6.

In the JSON and in the HSN CSV each unit is turned into the portal's unit code (UQC), such as NOS, KGS or MTR. A unit the portal does not know goes in as OTH (others).

**Something wrong?**
An **N/A** row: some items have no HSN code, and they are left out of the JSON. Add the code on those invoices and on the [product](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html#add-product). The same code on two rows means two rates or two units were used with it, which is correct.

### Document Summary — Table 13

The portal wants to know which document numbers you used in the period. One row per **number series** (the number without its last digits, such as INV/26-27/):

| Column | Meaning |

| Document Type | **Invoices for outward supply** (tax invoices, bills of supply, composition bills), **Credit notes** or **Delivery challans** |

| From, To | The lowest and highest number in that series this period |

| Total Issued | How many numbers were used, cancelled ones included |

| Cancelled | How many of those were cancelled. The portal works out net issued as Total minus Cancelled. |

Quotations and proforma estimates are not reported. If you changed the number prefix during the period, you see two rows: that is correct.

### GSTR-1 Summary Totals

The last card adds up the return: a **B2B Sales** row, a **B2C Sales** row, and a **Grand Total**. The Grand Total takes credit notes off, so it can be lower than B2B plus B2C. Exports are not in it (they are in GSTR-3B 3.1(b)).

After you upload the JSON, compare these figures with the summary the portal shows before you file.

### Exports and SEZ

- **Exports**: an invoice to a client whose country is not India. It is kept out of B2B and B2C and out of the JSON file, because the portal's export table (6A) can need the shipping bill number, date and port code, which the app does not record. The **Exports — Table 6A** table on the GSTR-1 tab lists them, ready to type into Table 6A on the portal: type **WPAY** (IGST paid) or **WOPAY** (under a LUT, no IGST), invoice number and date, rate, taxable value, IGST and invoice value. Exports saves the same rows as GSTR1_Exports_6A.csv. For services no shipping bill is needed; for goods add it on the portal.
- **SEZ units**: a client with **SEZ** ticked is a B2B sale, always inter-state. In the JSON it is an SEZ supply with payment of tax, or without payment if the invoice is under LUT.
- **GSTR-3B**: both exports and SEZ supplies are zero-rated, so their value (and IGST, if paid) goes in Table 3.1(b), not 3.1(a). See GSTR-3B.

Invoices in dollars, euros and other currencies
Every figure on this screen is in rupees. An invoice billed in another currency is turned into rupees at the exchange rate saved on that invoice (see [Billing in another currency](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#currency)): its value, taxable value and tax in every table, the HSN summary and GSTR-3B. The Exports table shows each invoice's currency and rate, for example USD @ 84.1.

An invoice in another currency **without** a rate cannot be turned into rupees. It is listed in the red box, its row in the Exports table shows no rate, and the GSTR-1 file is not made until you open the invoice and type the rate. Under GST the rate to use is the one for the date of the invoice: the RBI reference rate, or your bank's rate for that day.
