The rupee value is worked out from the invoice amounts and rounded to the paisa. If your accountant or the shipping bill uses a different rate, the portal figures follow theirs; ask them which to use.

## GSTR-1 downloads

The buttons at the top of the GSTR-1 tab:

| Button | What it saves |

| JSON Export | The file you upload to the portal: GSTR1_ GSTIN _ MMYYYY .json . It is checked first: see Checks before the file is made . |

| B2B | GSTR1_B2B_Invoices.csv : one row per B2B invoice, in the portal's Table 4A layout |

| B2C | GSTR1_B2C_Small.csv (totals by type, place of supply and rate), and GSTR1_B2C_Large.csv if there are any large invoices |

| HSN | GSTR1_HSN_Summary.csv , in the column order of the portal's Table 12 template, with the unit code (UQC) |

| CDNR | GSTR1_CDNR.csv for credit notes to registered clients, GSTR1_CDNUR.csv for unregistered |

| Docs | GSTR1_Doc_Summary.csv : the Table 13 rows |

| Mark Filed | Marks GSTR-1 filed for this period. The button goes away once it is marked; use the R1 pill to undo. |

The CSV files are for checking and for your CA. The JSON is what the portal takes. If there is nothing of that kind in the period you see a message such as "No B2B data to export" or "No Credit Notes", and no file is saved.

Files go to your browser's download folder. Download them again after changing an invoice: an old file does not update itself.

## Checks before the file is made

The portal rejects some mistakes outright, so JSON Export checks for them first.

**These stop the download until fixed** (the message starts "GSTR-1 export blocked — fix these first"):

- An invoice or credit note number longer than 16 characters, or with anything other than letters, digits, - or /. The message names the first three.
- An item with a GST rate the portal does not accept. The portal takes 0, 0.1, 0.25, 1, 1.5, 3, 5, 6, 7.5, 12, 18, 28 and 40%.
- Your own GSTIN is not set in [Settings, Company](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details).
- **Full year** is chosen as the period. A GSTR-1 file is for one month, or one quarter if you file quarterly.
- An invoice to a registered buyer, or an inter-state sale, with no place of supply (no client state and no Place of Supply on the invoice).

**These download with a warning** (the message starts "GSTR-1 JSON exported. ⚠"):

- Items with no HSN code. They are left out of the HSN table.
- HSN codes shorter than 4 digits, or 6 if you ticked turnover above ₹5 crore in [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#gstr-details).
- Custom units, which are sent as OTH (others).

**What the JSON holds:** B2B invoices, B2C totals, B2C Large invoices, credit notes to registered clients, credit notes to buyers without a GSTIN (a large inter-state one in Table 9B; the rest reduce the B2C totals), the HSN summary and the document summary. It is laid out the way the portal takes it today: from the May 2025 return, the HSN summary (Table 12) comes in two lists, **B2B** (buyers with a GSTIN, SEZ units too) and **B2C** (buyers without a GSTIN, and exports), each description at most 30 characters, and services with unit **NA** and quantity 0. Empty tables and blank values are left out, because the portal rejects them.

**What you add on the portal by hand:** exports (Table 6A), credit notes on exports, debit notes, advances received (Table 11), amendments to earlier periods (Table 9A), and nil-rated, exempt or non-GST sales (Table 8). Items at 0% are sent at a 0% rate in B2B and B2C.

**Something wrong?**
Blocked? Open each invoice the message names, correct the number or the rate, save, and export again. See ["GSTR-1 export blocked"](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#gstr1-blocked). "No invoices to export" means the period has no tax invoices or credit notes: check the period.

## Uploading GSTR-1 to the portal

- **Fix the red box**Clear the problems listed at the top first.
- **Download the JSON**JSON Export on the GSTR-1 tab, for the right month or quarter.
- **Open the return**Log in at gst.gov.in, go to **Returns Dashboard**, pick the financial year and period, and open GSTR-1.
- **Upload it**Choose **Prepare Offline**, upload the JSON, and wait for it to be processed. If the portal reports errors, it gives an error file to download: fix those invoices in the app and upload a fresh JSON.
- **Add what the file cannot hold**Exports in Table 6A, and anything else listed under What you add on the portal by hand.
- **Check and file**Compare the portal's summary with the app's Summary Totals, then submit and file with DSC or EVC (OTP).
- **Mark it filed**Back in the app, click Mark Filed.

## GSTR-3B: tax to pay

GSTR-3B is where you pay. The tab works it out in four steps: tax on sales (3.1 and 3.2), credit on purchases (4), the credit used against the tax (6), and what is left to pay in cash.

| Card | What it shows |

| Table 3.1 — Outward Supplies & Tax | (a) taxable sales, (b) exports with their IGST, (c) nil and exempt |

| Table 3.2 — Inter-state Supplies to Unregistered Persons | Inter-state B2C sales, by state. Shown only if there are any. |

| Table 4 — Eligible ITC | Credit from purchases and expenses, by IGST, CGST and SGST |

| Table 6 — Tax Payment Summary | Tax, credit used, **Net Tax Payable**, and credit carried forward |

| Net GST Payable | The one figure to pay |

The portal now fills most of GSTR-3B from your GSTR-1. Use the app's figures to check what it shows before you pay and file.

**Check the credit against GSTR-2B**
The credit here is everything you entered. Usually only what appears in your GSTR-2B can be claimed. Use the GSTR-2B Reconciliation tab to check.

Table **3.1(b) Zero-rated supplies** holds exports and supplies to SEZ units or developers, with or without IGST, in rupees. Supplies to an SEZ used to be counted in 3.1(a) with the other B2B sales; CBIC Circular 147/03/2021-GST (paragraph 3) treats that as a mistake that blocks the IGST refund, so they are now in 3.1(b). The IGST on them still counts in the tax you pay. Their credit notes reduce 3.1(b).

### Table 3.1 — Outward Supplies & Tax

| Row | What is in it |

| (a) Outward taxable supplies (other than zero-rated, nil-rated and exempted) | B2B and B2C sales, less credit notes: the same as the GSTR-1 Grand Total. Taxable value, IGST, CGST and SGST. |

| (b) Zero-rated supplies | Exports: their taxable value and any IGST charged on them |

| (c) Other outward supplies (nil rated, exempted) | Always ₹0: the app does not separate exempt sales. If you have them, enter them on the portal. |

Reverse-charge purchases, 3.1(d), are not shown on screen, but the 3B JSON fills them from the period's purchase bills marked reverse charge. Pay that tax in cash on the portal.

### Table 3.2 — Inter-state Supplies to Unregistered Persons

Appears only when you sold to a buyer without a GSTIN in another state. One row per state (the client's state), with the taxable value and IGST. It should agree with the inter-state rows of B2C Sales. On the portal, add a row for each place of supply.

### Table 4 — Eligible ITC (from Expenses & Purchases)

The GST you paid, which you can take off the GST you owe. It adds up:

- **[Purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html)** dated in the period: their GST goes to IGST if the purchase is marked inter-state, otherwise half to CGST and half to SGST.
- **[Expenses](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html#gst-credit)** dated in the period with a GST amount: the same way.

The row **(A) ITC Available — All other ITC** is the portal's Table 4(A)(5), where ordinary purchase credit goes. **Net ITC Available** is the same figure, because the app does not reverse any credit. Cess on purchases is sent in the 3B JSON.

**Not all GST paid is credit**
The app counts every GST amount you entered. Some is not claimable: food and drinks, personal spending, motor cars in most cases, bills without your GSTIN on them, or invoices the supplier has not reported (not in GSTR-2B). Leave such GST out of the expense, or reduce the figure on the portal. Ask your CA if unsure.

### Table 6 — Tax Payment Summary

| Row | Meaning |

| Output Tax Liability | Tax on your sales: Table 3.1(a), plus IGST on exports |

| Less: ITC utilised | The credit from Table 4 used against it, in the order the law sets |

| Net Tax Payable | What is left, for each tax and in total. This is paid in cash. |

| ITC carried forward | Shown only when credit is left over. It stays in your credit ledger for next month. |

Credit is used in the order the law sets: IGST credit first (against IGST, then CGST and SGST), then CGST credit (against CGST, then IGST) and SGST credit (against SGST, then IGST). CGST credit never pays SGST, nor SGST credit CGST. So credit you hold in CGST and SGST can pay a tax that is all IGST. When IGST credit is spread over CGST and SGST, the app sends it first to the part your own CGST or SGST credit cannot cover, so none of that credit is left stranded while you pay cash.

**Example.** You owe CGST ₹9,000 and SGST ₹9,000, and no IGST. You have IGST credit ₹5,000 and CGST credit ₹6,000. CGST credit can cover only ₹6,000 of the CGST, so IGST credit pays the other ₹3,000 of CGST and its last ₹2,000 goes to SGST. CGST credit pays its ₹6,000. You pay SGST ₹7,000 in cash, and nothing is carried forward.

If instead you owed only SGST ₹9,000 and had CGST credit ₹6,000, that credit could not be used at all: you would pay ₹9,000 in cash and carry ₹6,000 CGST credit forward.

### Net GST Payable

The big figure at the bottom of the GSTR-3B tab: the total to pay for the period. Underneath it says **Pay via Electronic Cash Ledger** (create a challan on the portal and pay by net banking, UPI, card or NEFT/RTGS), or **ITC covers your liability** when nothing is due in cash.

Late payment carries interest at 18% a year on the cash amount, and a late fee for filing late. See the Filing Guide.

### GSTR-3B downloads

| Button | What it saves |

| 3B CSV | GSTR3B_Summary.csv : rows for 3.1(a), 4(A) ITC available, 6.1 ITC utilised, 6.1 tax payable in cash, and ITC carried forward |

| 3B JSON | GSTR3B_ GSTIN _ MMYYYY .json in the portal's GSTR-3B format: 3.1(a), 3.1(b), reverse charge 3.1(d) and Table 4(A)(5) with cess. Other rows are sent as 0. |

| Mark Filed | Marks GSTR-3B filed for this period; use the 3B pill to undo |

3B JSON says "No data to export for this period" when the period has no invoices and no expenses, even if it has purchase bills. In that case use 3B CSV, or type the credit in on the portal.

## Checking your credit against GSTR-2B

GSTR-2B lists the invoices your suppliers reported. The **GSTR-2B Reconciliation** tab compares it with the [purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html) you entered, so you claim only credit that is really there. (If the tab is missing, turn on **GSTR-2B matching** in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features).)

- **Download GSTR-2B**On the portal: **Returns**, **GSTR-2B**, pick the month, **Download JSON**. If it comes as a ZIP, extract it.
- **Pick the same period here**Choose the same month at the top of GST Returns.
- **Import it**Click Import 2B JSON and choose the file. A message says "Imported GSTR-2B for GSTIN — N suppliers".
- **Read the results**Each 2B entry is matched to your purchase bills by the supplier's GSTIN and invoice number. See Reading the results.
- **Act on the differences**Correct your bills, add missing ones, or ask suppliers to file.

Before you import, the tab shows "Import your GSTR-2B JSON to reconcile against your purchase records." If you have no purchase bills at all, it warns that everything will show as "2B only".

The imported file is not kept: import it again after leaving the screen. Only the B2B invoices in GSTR-2B are compared (not its credit notes, imports or ISD entries), and only purchase bills, not expenses.

**Something wrong?**
"That doesn't look like a GSTR-2B JSON": you picked the Excel or PDF, or another return. See [the GSTR-2B file message](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#gstr2b-wrong-file).

### Reading the GSTR-2B results

After an import you see Export reconciliation CSV, Clear (removes the imported file), and "Imported for GSTIN · period MMYYYY". Check that period matches the one you picked.

The row of counts below works as a filter: click one to show only those rows, or **Total entries** to show all.

| Status | Meaning | What to do |

| **✓ Matched** | In both, and the invoice value and taxable value agree to within ₹1 | Nothing. This credit is safe to claim. |

| **⚠ Amount mismatch** | In both, but the amounts differ by more than ₹1 | Compare with the paper bill. Correct your purchase entry, or ask the supplier to amend their GSTR-1. |

| **⚠ Books only** | A purchase bill of this period that is not in GSTR-2B | The supplier may not have filed, or filed with a different number or GSTIN. Ask them. Usually you cannot claim it until it appears. |

| **⚠ 2B only** | In GSTR-2B but not in your purchase bills | Enter the bill in [Purchases](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#add-purchase) if it is yours. If you never bought it, tell the supplier. |

The table shows Status, Supplier (name and GSTIN), Invoice No., Date, **2B Value**, **Books Value**, **Diff** (2B minus books, in red when more than ₹1) and **ITC**: ✓ when GSTR-2B says the credit is available, ✗ when it is not (Books only rows always show ✗).

How matching works: invoice numbers are compared ignoring capitals, spaces, slashes and dashes, so INV/12 matches inv-12. Your book value includes cess and any round-off on the bill. A bill entered in an earlier month still matches; only this period's bills can show as Books only.

## TDS and TCS report

The **TDS / TCS Report** tab adds up the period's tax invoices and credit notes that have [TDS or TCS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#tds-tcs) on them. These are income-tax amounts, not GST. It has two cards.

The CSV files list every invoice with quarter, section, rate, client, GSTIN, PAN, taxable value and amount. They are for your CA to prepare Form 26Q and Form 27EQ from (filed through tin-nsdl.com); they are not the forms themselves.

**Something wrong?**
A card says "No invoices with TDS in this period": no invoice in the period has TDS turned on. Turn it on in the invoice under Customize, then TDS, and save. Check the period too: for a quarterly figure pick **Quarterly**.

### TDS Receivable (deducted by clients)

Tax your clients should have deducted from what they pay you, under sections such as 194C, 194J or 194Q. You claim it against your own income tax, so check it shows in your Form 26AS / AIS.

- Three figures: **Invoices with TDS**, **Taxable value**, **Total TDS receivable**.
- A table by **Quarter** (Q1 is April–June) and **Section**, with the number of invoices, taxable value and TDS. An invoice with no section chosen is counted under 194Q.
- Export TDS CSV saves TDS_Receivable_Report.csv. It is greyed out when there is nothing to export.

### TCS Collected (from clients)

Tax you collected from buyers on top of the invoice. You must deposit it with the Income Tax Department and report it in Form 27EQ every quarter.

- Three figures: **Invoices with TCS**, **Taxable value**, **Total TCS collected**.
- A table by quarter and section. An invoice with no section chosen is counted under 206C(1H).
- Export TCS CSV saves TCS_Collected_Report.csv.

## The Filing Guide tab

Step-by-step portal instructions inside the app. At the top a one-line reminder: review the GSTR-1 and 3B tabs, export the JSON, upload it, file GSTR-1 first and GSTR-3B after, with the usual due dates (GSTR-1 by the 11th, GSTR-3B by the 20th of the next month) and the late fee.

Three buttons switch what is shown:

| Button | What it shows |

| Regular Filing (With Sales) | GSTR-1 in 9 steps, GSTR-1 Pro Tips, GSTR-3B in 7 steps, GSTR-3B Pro Tips |

| NIL Return (No Sales) | When a NIL return applies, and how to file NIL GSTR-1 and NIL GSTR-3B. See NIL returns . |

| Common Errors & Fixes | Portal error messages and what to do, and key GST rules |

Click a step to open its details. Tick the circle at the left of a step as you finish it: it turns green and is struck through. The ticks are not saved.

Due dates, fees and rules in the guide are as the app knows them; the government changes them from time to time, so confirm on gst.gov.in or with your CA.

### GSTR-1 steps in the Filing Guide

The card **GSTR-1 — Sales Return (File This First)** walks through the portal:

- Log in to the GST portal.
- Select the return period, and choose Prepare Online or Prepare Offline.
- Table 4A, B2B invoices: what each portal field means.
- Table 5, B2C Large.
- Table 7, B2C (Others), entered as totals.
- Table 9B, credit and debit notes.
- Table 12, HSN summary, and how many digits your turnover needs.
- Table 13, documents issued.
- Preview, submit and file with DSC or EVC, and keep the ARN.

If you upload the app's JSON, steps 3 to 8 are already filled in: just check them.

### GSTR-3B steps in the Filing Guide

The card **GSTR-3B — Summary Return + Tax Payment (File After GSTR-1)**: open GSTR-3B, check Table 3.1 and 3.2, claim credit in Table 4, Table 5 (exempt and non-GST purchases), Table 6 (paying the tax, and the order credit is used), then submit, pay and file. The last step lists what happens if you file late: a late fee per day, 18% a year interest on tax paid late, the next return blocked, and e-way bills blocked after two months.

### GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B Pro Tips

Two green and blue boxes in Regular Filing with practical tips: the quickest way to upload GSTR-1 (the JSON), opting for quarterly filing (QRMP) under ₹5 crore, where amendments, exports and advances go, why to check GSTR-2B before claiming credit, the order credit is used, how to pay through a challan, how interest is worked out, and where reverse-charge tax goes.

### Common GST Portal Errors & How to Fix Them

The card under Common Errors & Fixes lists the portal messages people meet most, each with the fix: Invalid GSTIN, invoice number already exists, place of supply mismatch, invoice date outside the return period, invalid HSN code, GSTR-3B blocked because GSTR-1 is not filed, credit more than GSTR-2B, previous period not filed, taxable value and tax mismatch, EVC or OTP problems, and challan amount not matching.

For messages from the app itself, see [Troubleshooting, GST and returns](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#gst-returns-problems).

### Key GST Rules to Remember

A short list of the rules behind the returns: the time limit to claim credit (Section 16(4)), the time limit for credit notes (Section 34), when an invoice must be issued (Section 31), the order credit is used (Section 49), credit only as in GSTR-2B, interest on late payment (Section 50), how long notices can come (Sections 73 and 74, keep records at least 6 years), cancellation of GSTIN for not filing (Section 29(2)(c)), and e-way bills blocked for unfiled GSTR-3B.

## NIL returns

If a period has no invoices, no purchase bills and no expenses, an amber banner says: "No invoices, purchase bills or expenses found — file a NIL return on the GST portal. NIL returns are mandatory."

A NIL return is only right when you had no sales, no credit to claim, no tax due and no reverse-charge purchases. A period with a purchase bill has credit to claim, so the banner does not appear: file a regular GSTR-3B for it. (A NIL GSTR-1 may still be right if you sold nothing.)

- **Open the NIL guide**On the Filing Guide tab, click NIL Return (No Sales). The box **When to File NIL Return** lists the conditions.
- **File NIL GSTR-1 first**Follow **NIL GSTR-1 — File First (Even with Zero Sales)**: open GSTR-1, check every table is empty, and file.
- **Then NIL GSTR-3B**Follow **NIL GSTR-3B — File After NIL GSTR-1**: check all values are zero, submit and file.
- **Or by SMS**NIL returns can also be filed by SMS to **14409** from the authorised signatory's registered mobile. Send NIL R1 <GSTIN> <MMYYYY> for GSTR-1, NIL 3B <GSTIN> <MMYYYY> for GSTR-3B, or NIL C8 <GSTIN> <MMYYYY> for CMP-08, for example NIL 3B 29ABCDE1234F1ZW 092026. A quarterly return uses the quarter's last month. You get a code back: reply CNF 3B <code> (or CNF R1, CNF C8) within 30 minutes. The **NIL Return Quick Summary** box shows the same formats. Source: the GST portal's [SMS filing FAQs](https://tutorial.gst.gov.in/userguide/returns/faq_nilreturngstr3b.htm).
- **Mark both filed**Click the R1 and 3B pills at the top.

File on time even with nothing to report: late fees still apply, and not filing for six months can get your GSTIN cancelled.

## E-invoicing (IRN)

A business whose yearly turnover (aggregate, all GSTINs on one PAN) has been above **₹5 crore** in any year since 2017-18 must register its B2B invoices on the e-invoice portal. The portal gives each invoice an **IRN** (Invoice Reference Number) and a signed QR code, and an invoice without them is not valid. Below ₹5 crore you do not need any of this.

The app stays offline: it makes the file, you upload it, and you bring the IRN back. Turn on **E-invoicing (IRN)** in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features) first; it is off to start.

- **Download the e-invoice JSON**For one invoice: open it, click E-invoice in the toolbar, then Download e-invoice JSON. For several: tick them on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#bulk) and click E-invoice JSON in the bar that appears. Save the invoice first, so its number is final.
- **Upload it on the portal**Log in at einvoice1.gst.gov.in, go to **e-Invoice**, **Bulk Upload**, choose the file and upload it. The portal returns the IRN, Ack No, Ack Date and Signed QR Code for each invoice; download that result as JSON.
- **Bring the IRN back**On the Dashboard, click Import IRN and choose that JSON file. Each IRN is saved on the invoice with the same number, date and GSTIN. Or open one invoice, click E-invoice, paste the four values and click Save IRN.

From then on every design, A4 to thermal, prints **IRN**, **Ack No**, **Ack Date** and the QR code at the top of the invoice. The Dashboard marks such invoices **IRN**. Importing the IRN changes nothing else on the invoice.

**What goes in the file:** tax invoices and credit notes to clients with a GSTIN, SEZ units and clients abroad (exports), in rupees. A credit note names its original invoice when that number is in the app. The amounts are the ones printed on the invoice, to the paisa. TCS goes in as other charges; a discount on the whole bill goes in as the invoice discount.

**What is checked first.** Invoices with a problem are left out of the file and listed with what to fix:

- a client with no GSTIN (a sale to a consumer needs no e-invoice), or a GSTIN that looks mistyped;
- a missing PIN code, city, address or state, yours or the client's (yours are in [Settings, Company Details](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details));
- an item with no HSN/SAC code, or one that is not 4, 6 or 8 digits; an item name shorter than 3 letters; a GST rate the portal does not accept;
- an invoice number longer than 16 characters, with anything other than letters, digits, / and -, or starting with 0, / or -;
- a date in the future, a cancelled invoice, an invoice in another currency, an invoice that charges no GST, or one that already has an IRN.

**Changing an invoice after its IRN**
The portal does not take changes to a registered invoice. Cancel it on the portal within 24 hours and make a new one, or issue a credit note. The app warns you when you open an invoice that has an IRN.

Businesses with turnover of ₹10 crore or more must report an invoice within 30 days of its date, or the portal refuses it.

### The E-invoice (IRN) window

Opens from E-invoice in the invoice toolbar (only while E-invoicing is on, and for tax invoices and credit notes). At the top it repeats the three steps: download, upload on einvoice1.gst.gov.in (e-Invoice → Bulk Upload), paste the reply.

Below that, one notice tells you where you stand:

| Notice | Meaning |

| "Save the invoice first, so its number is final." | The invoice is new or unsaved. Save it, then open this window again. The download and Save IRN stay greyed out until then. |

| "**Fix these first:**" and a list | Problems the portal would reject, such as a missing PIN code or HSN code. Fix each one on the invoice or in Settings, save, and reopen. Download e-invoice JSON is greyed out until the list is empty. |

| "This invoice has its IRN…" | The IRN is saved and prints on the invoice. |

| Field or button | What to know |

| Download e-invoice JSON | Saves EINV- invoice number .json (slashes become dashes) for upload on the portal |

| **IRN** | 64 letters and digits (0-9, a-f), from the portal's reply |

| **Ack No** | The acknowledgement number, 10 to 20 digits |

| **Ack Date** | As the portal shows it |

| **Signed QR Code** | The long text that starts with eyJ . Copy all of it: it has three parts separated by dots, and it must be for the same IRN. |

| Save IRN | Checks the four values and saves them on the invoice. "IRN saved. It now prints on the invoice." confirms it. A mistake is listed in red under the fields. |

| Remove IRN | Only when an IRN is saved. Takes it off the invoice (for example, after you cancelled the e-invoice on the portal). |

| Close | Closes without saving |

**Something wrong?**
"The Signed QR Code is not complete": part of it was missed when copying. Copy it again from the first character to the last. "The Signed QR Code is for a different IRN": the IRN and QR code came from two different invoices.

### E-invoice results: invoices left out, IRNs not saved

After E-invoice JSON or Import IRN on the Dashboard, a window lists any invoice that was not handled, each with the reason. Its title tells you what happened:

| Title | Meaning |

| "N invoices were left out" | The file was made, but without these. Fix each one, then export them again. |

| "Nothing was exported" | None of the ticked invoices could go in the file. The reasons are listed. |

| "IRN saved on N invoices; M not saved" | Some IRNs from the portal's file were saved, the rest were not |

| "No IRN was saved" | None of the IRNs in the file matched an invoice |

Usual reasons an IRN is not saved:

- "No invoice … for this business was found": the number or date differs, or a different business is selected in the sidebar.
- "More than one invoice … was found": paste the IRN into the right invoice by hand.
- "The file does not say which invoice this IRN is for": paste it by hand.
- "Already saved on this invoice", or "This invoice already has a different IRN. It was not changed."

Click OK to close. If the whole file is refused with "No IRN was found in that file", you chose the wrong file: pick the JSON the e-invoice portal gave back after upload.

---

# Reports

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/reports.html

Profit and loss, who owes you and for how long, party outstanding by month, your best clients, your best-selling products, closing stock with its value, TDS and TCS, and profit by branch or project. Every report prints and downloads as Excel or CSV.

## The report tabs

Open Reports from the sidebar. A row of buttons at the top picks the report; the one you are on is filled in blue. The small ? at the end of that row opens the part of this guide for the report you are looking at.

| Tab | What it answers | Period |

| Profit & Loss | Did I make money? Sales minus expenses, without GST, and month by month. | The period you choose |

| Outstanding & Aging | Who owes me money today, on which invoice, and how late is it? | Every unpaid invoice, any date |

| Party Outstanding | The same money owed, one row per party and one column per month, the way Tally shows it. | A financial or calendar year |

| Client Analytics | Who are my best customers, and who pays slowest? | The period you choose |

| Product Performance | What sells most, by money and by quantity? | The period you choose |

| Stock | How much of each product did I have at the end of a month, and what was it worth? | The month you choose |

| TDS & TCS | Which clients deducted TDS from my sales, have their certificates come, what TCS did I collect, and what TDS did I deduct from suppliers? | A financial year, a quarter or your own dates |

| By cost centre | What did each branch, site or project sell, spend and earn? Shows only when cost centres are turned on. | The period you choose |

Reports always open on Profit & Loss. Which tab you were on is not remembered after you leave the screen.

## What the reports include

The sales tabs cover the business selected at the top of the sidebar, and count only real sales, as the Dashboard does:

- **Counted:** tax invoices, bills of supply and composition bills.
- **Subtracted:** credit notes (goods returned or a discount given after the sale) reduce the sales of the period they are dated in.
- **Left out:** proforma invoices and estimates (a quote is not a sale), delivery challans (goods moved, not sold) and cancelled invoices.

Purchase bills are not part of these reports, except By cost centre; they are in [Income Tax, ITR Summary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/income-tax.html#itr-summary) and the [purchase register](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#export). Expenses are counted in Profit & Loss and By cost centre.

Two exceptions to "this business only":

- **Stock** covers every business, because products and stock are shared by all your businesses.
- To see another business's reports, switch business at the top of the sidebar (see [More than one business](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#multiple-businesses)).

**GST in plain words**GST you charge on a sale is not your money: you collect it for the government. GST you pay on purchases and expenses usually comes back as input tax credit (ITC). So Profit & Loss, Product Performance and By cost centre show amounts **without GST**. Client Analytics and the outstanding reports show the full invoice amount **with GST**, because that is what the customer owes you. See the [glossary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/glossary.html#terms) for GST words.

## Choosing the period and currency

Profit & Loss, Client Analytics, Product Performance and By cost centre share one period box at the top. Change it on one tab and the others follow. (Outstanding & Aging, Party Outstanding and Stock have their own choices, described in their sections.)

| Box | What it does |

| **Filter By** | **Fiscal Year** (1 April to 31 March) or **Month / Year** (one calendar month). |

| **Fiscal Year** | Shows with Fiscal Year. The current financial year and the four before it, such as FY 2026-27. It starts on the current one. |

| **Month** and **Year** | Show with Month / Year. Any month of this year or the five years before. They start on the current month. |

| **Currency** | Shows only when invoices in the period are in more than one currency, for example rupees and US dollars for export. Different currencies are never added together; pick one and the tab shows only invoices (and expenses) in it. |

The small ? at the end of this box opens this section.

**Something wrong?**A figure looks too small or is zero: check the period (a month you have not billed in shows nothing), the business at the top of the sidebar, and the currency. An invoice dated 31 March belongs to the financial year that ends that day, not the next one.

If you bill in more than one currency, the **Currency** list starts with **All, in ₹** (the default): every invoice is counted, a foreign-currency one in rupees at the exchange rate saved on it, so export income is in your profit and loss with your rupee expenses. Pick one currency to see only its invoices, in that currency. Invoices with no exchange rate are left out of **All, in ₹** and named above the statement, so you can add the rate.

## Printing and downloading a report

Every report table has three buttons at its top right:

| Button | What you get |

| Print / PDF | Opens the table alone in a new window, with its title and a line saying the business and period, and the print box opens. Choose your printer, or **Save as PDF** as the printer to keep a PDF. Wide reports (outstanding, party outstanding, cost centres) print landscape. |

| Excel | Downloads an .xlsx file. Amounts are real numbers, so Excel can total, sort and filter them. |

| CSV | The same table as a CSV file, for any spreadsheet, Tally import or your CA's software. |

They export what the screen shows: the period, currency and filters you chose, with a **Total** row where the screen has one. Files go to your browser's Downloads folder, named after the report and period, such as Profit-and-loss-FY_2026-27.xlsx.

The Expense statement and Purchase register have the same three buttons on their own screens.

**Something wrong?****"Nothing to export"**: the table is empty for that period; choose another period. **"Allow pop-ups for this page to print the report"**: the browser blocked the print window; allow pop-ups for the app and click again (see [Print does nothing](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#print-blocked)). Excel shows odd characters in a CSV: use the Excel button instead.

## Profit & Loss

Did the business make money in the period? Choose the period in the box at the top (see Choosing the period). If you bill in more than one currency, a **Currency** choice appears, since different currencies are never added together.

Four cards at the top give the answer:

| Card | What it is |

| **Revenue (ex. tax)** | Your sales without GST (and without any TCS collected on the invoices). Credit notes are subtracted. |

| **Expenses (ex. GST)** | Your [expenses](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html) without the GST on them. |

| **Net Profit** or **Net Loss** | Revenue minus expenses. Green for a profit; red with a minus sign for a loss. |

| **Margin** | Profit as a percentage of revenue. ₹20,000 profit on ₹1,00,000 revenue is a 20% margin. |

Purchase bills (stock you bought to sell) are **not** subtracted here; this is sales less expenses. For profit after purchases, use By cost centre (its Total row is the whole business) or [Income Tax, ITR Summary](https://billing.reazix.com/help/income-tax.html#itr-summary).

The same period choice appears on the Client Analytics and Product Performance tabs.

### Profit & Loss Statement

The card below the four figures sets the sum out line by line, the way an accountant would:

| Line | Meaning |

| **Total Revenue** | Everything billed in the period, GST included, less credit notes. |

| **Less: GST Collected** | The GST (and TCS) on those invoices. It belongs to the government. |

| **Net Revenue** | What you actually earned from sales. |

| **Total Expenses** | Expenses with their GST. |

| **Less: GST on Expenses (ITC)** | The GST on those expenses, which comes back to you as input tax credit. |

| **Net Expenses** | What the expenses really cost you. |

| **Net Profit** / **Net Loss** | Net Revenue minus Net Expenses. |

With more than one currency, the card says **Showing USD invoices only** (or whichever currency you picked).

**Something wrong?**Profit looks too high: purchases are not subtracted on this tab (see above), and an expense entered without its GST split counts in full. Revenue looks too low: check that the invoices are not saved as proforma or challans, and are not cancelled.

### Monthly Breakdown

One row for each month that had sales or expenses in the period, oldest first, with **Revenue**, **Expenses** and **Profit/Loss** for that month, all without GST. A profit shows in green, a loss in red. Months with nothing in them are left out.

The card appears only when the period has some activity. Print / PDF, Excel and CSV export it with a **Total** row at the bottom.

- **Pick the year**Filter By **Fiscal Year**, and the year.
- **Read the months**Look for months in red: those are the months you spent more than you sold.
- **Send it to your CA**Click Excel and email the file.

## Outstanding & Aging

Every unpaid or part-paid sales invoice, whatever its date, grouped by how late it is. Use it each week to decide whom to call first. The period box does not apply here: this is what is owed **today**.

Five cards at the top:

| Card | Money owed on invoices that are |

| **Total Outstanding** | All of them added up |

| **Current (0-30d)** | Not yet due, or up to 30 days past the due date (green) |

| **31-60 days** | 31 to 60 days late (amber) |

| **61-90 days** | 61 to 90 days late (purple) |

| **90+ days** | More than 90 days late (red): the ones to chase first |

Days are counted from the invoice's **due date**; an invoice with no due date counts from its invoice date. If you have invoices in more than one currency, there is one row of cards for each currency, labelled INR, USD and so on.

What "outstanding" means: the invoice total, less any TDS your client deducted (they pay you the Net Receivable), less what they have paid so far. Invoices marked paid, and credit notes, estimates, challans and cancelled invoices are not listed.

**Filter by client name...** narrows the table and the five cards together. Type part of a name, such as "shar" for Sharma Traders; the × clears it.

### Outstanding Receivables

The table lists each unpaid invoice, the most overdue at the top:

| Column | Meaning |

| **Client** | Who owes it |

| **Invoice No**, **Date**, **Due Date** | Which invoice, and when it was due |

| **Amount** | The invoice total, with GST |

| **Paid** | What they paid so far (a dash if nothing) |

| **Outstanding** | What is still owed, in red |

| **Days Overdue** | **Current** if not late yet, otherwise the days late, such as **45d**. Rows more than 30 days late are highlighted, and more than 90 days late even more strongly. |

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV export the list (landscape), with a **Currency** column and the date "unpaid as on" in the title line. Handy for a collection round or to send to a salesman.

- **Find who to call**Read the 90+ days card, then the red rows at the top of the table.
- **Record the money when it comes**Record the payment on the [Dashboard](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payments) or make a [receipt](https://billing.reazix.com/help/receipts.html#new-receipt). The invoice drops off this list once it is fully paid.

**Something wrong?**An invoice the client has paid still shows: the payment was not recorded in the app. Record it on the Dashboard. "No outstanding receivables found." with money owed: check the business at the top of the sidebar, and clear the client filter. For one client's full account, see their [ledger](https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html#ledger).

## Party Outstanding

The same money owed, laid out the way Tally does it: one row per party (client), A to Z, one column per month, a **Total** for each party on the right and a **Total** for each month at the bottom. Each unpaid amount sits in the month of its invoice, so you can see at a glance that, say, Mehta Traders still owes ₹12,000 from June and ₹8,500 from August.

The card is titled **Party outstanding by month**. Its boxes:

| Box | What it does |

| **Financial year (Apr-Mar)** / **Calendar year (Jan-Dec)** | Twelve columns from April to March (the default), or January to December. |

| Year | Which year: FY 2026-27 and the five before it, or 2026 and the five before it. |

| Currency | Shows only when you have invoices in more than one currency. |

- Bills from before that year that are still unpaid appear in an **Earlier** column at the start, so nothing owed drops out of the total. The column shows only when there is something in it.
- Invoices dated after the year you chose are not shown.
- The Party column and the Total column stay in place while you scroll sideways through the months.
- Print / PDF opens the table on its own page, landscape; choose your printer or Save as PDF. Excel and CSV download it.

Only sales count; estimates, challans and cancelled invoices are left out, and TDS the client deducted is taken off. Credit notes are **not** subtracted here (as on Outstanding & Aging).

**Something wrong?**"Nobody owes you anything for FY ..." while money is owed: the invoices may be from after that year (pick a later year) or in another currency (pick it in the currency box). The same customer shows twice: the client name is spelt differently on the invoices (capital letters and spaces at the start or end are ignored, other differences are not).

### What you owe suppliers

The same table the other way round. In the first box of the card, pick **You owe suppliers** (it starts on **Clients owe you**). The card is then titled **Owed to suppliers by month**: one row per supplier, A to Z, with what you still have to pay them in the month of their bill, an **Earlier** column for older unpaid bills, and totals.

- What is owed on a bill is its total, less TDS you keep back, less the [payments recorded on it](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#record-payment). A Paid bill is left out.
- A bill marked Paid before payments could be recorded owes nothing. A bill marked Partial then, with no payments recorded, shows its whole amount.
- Purchase bills are in rupees, so there is no currency box.
- Print / PDF, Excel and CSV save it, titled "Owed to suppliers".

**Something wrong?**"You owe no supplier anything for FY ..." while you do: the bills may be dated after that year, or marked Paid. The same supplier shows twice: their name is spelt differently on the bills.

## Client Analytics

Who buys the most, and who owes the most, in the period chosen at the top. Revenue here includes GST (it is what the client was billed), less their credit notes.

### Top clients by revenue

The ten clients who were billed the most in the period, highest first, with **Revenue** and the number of **Invoices** (credit notes are not counted as invoices). Use it to know whom to look after: a discount or a call to your best ten pays back the most.

"No client data for this period." means there were no sales in that period and currency.

### Highest outstanding (worst payers)

The ten clients who owe you the most on invoices from this period, with **Outstanding** and **% Unpaid**: what share of what they were billed is still unpaid. 80% unpaid is a customer to stop giving credit to. Outstanding is after any TDS they deducted.

"Everyone is up to date." means nobody owes anything on this period's invoices. For money owed from any date, see Outstanding & Aging.

### All clients breakdown

Every client billed in the period, the number in brackets being how many. Columns: **Client**, **Invoices**, **Revenue**, **Paid**, **Outstanding** (a dash if nothing), **Last Invoice** date. Highest revenue first. Print / PDF, Excel and CSV export it.

**Something wrong?**One customer appears on two rows: the name is typed differently on some invoices ("Sharma Traders" and "Sharma Traders Pvt Ltd"). Clients are grouped by the exact name on the invoice. To see one client's whole history, open their [ledger](https://billing.reazix.com/help/clients.html#ledger).

## Product Performance

What you sold, by item, in the period chosen at the top. Revenue here is the line's taxable value: after line discounts and without GST, so it matches your invoices. Credit notes are subtracted (returned quantities come off too). Delivery charges and other charge lines are not a product and are left out. Items are grouped by the name on the invoice line.

### Top revenue producers

The ten items that brought in the most money, with **Revenue** and **Qty sold**. Rest the mouse on a name to see its HSN code. "No product data for this period." means no sales in that period.

### Most units sold

The ten items sold in the largest quantity, with **Qty sold** and **Txns** (on how many invoice lines it appeared). A cheap item that sells in large numbers shows here even if it is not in the revenue top ten. Quantities of different units (kg, pieces, boxes) are not converted, so compare like with like.

### All products

Every item sold in the period, the number in brackets being how many, highest revenue first:

| Column | Meaning |

| **Product** | The item name as on the invoice |

| **HSN** | The HSN or SAC code (the GST code for the goods or service), from the first invoice line that has one |

| **Qty sold** | Total quantity, less returns |

| **Revenue** | Taxable value, without GST |

| **Avg rate** | Revenue ÷ quantity: the average price you really got |

| **Txns** | Number of invoice lines |

| **Last sold** | Date of the latest invoice with it |

Print / PDF, Excel and CSV export it.

**Something wrong?**The same item appears twice: it was typed with different names on different invoices. Pick items from the [product list](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html) when billing so the name is always the same. A product you sold is missing: lines with no item name are not counted.

## Stock

Closing stock of every product at the end of a month, and what it is worth. Useful at year end (closing stock for your accounts or a bank loan), and to check stock against the shelf. The card is titled **Closing stock as on** and the date.

Choose the month in the box next to the title: this month and the 35 before it. A past month shows its last day; the current month shows today's stock.

| Column | Meaning |

| **Product**, **HSN/SAC**, **Unit** | From the [product list](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html), A to Z. Unit shows Nos when none is set. |

| **Closing qty** | Worked back from today's stock, using the dates of your invoices, purchase bills and [production entries](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html#manufacturing). Negative stock shows in red. |

| **Rate** | The purchase price. A product with no purchase price is valued at its selling price, marked with *. |

| **Value** | Quantity × rate. A dash for zero or negative stock. |

| **Total stock value** | The bottom row: all the values added up. Negative stock is not added in. |

Stock you typed in by hand on the Products screen has no date, so it counts as if it changed today. Products are shared by all your businesses, so this report covers every business. Print / PDF, Excel and CSV export it, "valued at purchase price".

**Something wrong?**A red (negative) quantity means more was sold than was bought: a purchase bill is missing, or opening stock was never entered. Add the purchase, or correct the stock on the [Products](https://billing.reazix.com/help/products.html#stock) screen. Values marked * use the selling price: add a purchase price to the product for a true value. "No products yet." means the product list is empty; stock is tracked only for items in it. See also [what stock does not do](https://billing.reazix.com/help/limitations.html#stock-limits).

## TDS & TCS

Three lists of tax that is cut from, or added to, a payment, so you can match your books with the income tax department's records and with your CA's returns. Open Reports and click TDS & TCS. New to TDS and TCS? Read [GST basics: TDS and TCS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-basics.html#tds-tcs) first; it explains them with an example.

In plain words:

- **TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)**: when a business client pays you for contract work, professional fees, rent, commission and the like, it keeps back a small part (for example 10% under 194J) as income tax and deposits it against **your PAN**. That money is not lost: you claim it in your income tax return.
- **TCS (Tax Collected at Source)**: tax you add to your own invoice and collect from the buyer, for example under CGST section 52 if you run an online marketplace. You deposit it with the government.
- **TDS you deduct**: when you pay a contractor or professional above the limits, you keep back TDS from their bill and deposit it yourself, then file a quarterly TDS return (Form 26Q).

**Choose the period** at the top: a **Financial year**, then **Whole year**, one quarter (**Q1** April to June, **Q2** July to September, **Q3** October to December, **Q4** January to March) or **Custom dates** with From and To. TDS returns and certificates go quarter by quarter, so a quarter is usually what you want. Like the other reports, it covers the business selected at the top of the sidebar; cancelled invoices, quotations, proformas and challans are left out.

Four cards at the top give the totals: **TDS by your clients**, **Certificates received** (ticked out of all), **TCS you collected** and **TDS you deducted**. Each list has Print / PDF, Excel and CSV buttons for your CA.

**Something wrong?**An invoice is missing from the TDS list: TDS was not ticked on it. Open it and tick TDS under Customize (see [TDS and TCS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/invoices.html#tds-tcs)), or record the TDS with the client's payment (see [TDS when recording a payment](https://billing.reazix.com/help/dashboard.html#payment-tds)). A purchase bill is missing: tick **TDS deducted** on it (see [TDS on a purchase bill](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#purchase-tds)). The GST Returns screen has a similar [TDS / TCS tab](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-returns.html#tds-tcs) with Form 26Q / 27EQ figures.

### TDS deducted by your clients

One row per sales invoice on which the client deducts TDS: **Date**, **Invoice No**, **Client**, the client's **PAN** (read from its GSTIN), the **Section** (194J, 194C...), **Rate**, the **Taxable** value it is worked out on (the value before GST) and the **TDS** amount. Under the list, **By client** and **By quarter** add them up.

**How to reconcile it.** The TDS a client deducts reaches your PAN only when the client deposits it and files its own TDS return. Check it once a quarter:

- **Pick the quarter**Choose the financial year and, say, **Q2 (Jul-Sep)**.
- **Open your tax statement**Log in at [incometax.gov.in](https://www.incometax.gov.in/) and open **Form 26AS** (Form 168 from tax year 2026-27) or the **AIS** (Annual Information Statement). They list the TDS every client deposited against your PAN.
- **Tick what matches**When an invoice's TDS shows there, or the client sends its **TDS certificate (Form 16A)**, tick the box in the **Certificate** column. The tick is saved on the invoice at once and is kept if you edit the invoice later.
- **Chase the rest**An unticked row after the quarter's due date means that client has not deposited or filed yet. Ask them: until it shows in your tax statement you cannot claim it.
- **Claim it**Give the year's total (and the Excel file) to your CA for your income tax return.

Form 16A is the certificate for payments up to 31 March 2026; under the Income-tax Act, 2025 the certificate has a new form, but it does the same job. See [A client deducts income-tax TDS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-basics.html#income-tax-tds).

### TCS you collected

One row per sales invoice with TCS: the same columns as above, with the **TCS** amount, and totals **By client** and **By quarter**. This is money you collected for the government: deposit it and report it in your TCS return (Form 27EQ for income-tax TCS; GSTR-8 for GST TCS under CGST section 52). Since 10 July 2024 the section 52 rate is 0.5% (it was 1%); new invoices start at 0.5%, older ones keep the rate they were made with. See [GST TDS and GST TCS](https://billing.reazix.com/help/gst-basics.html#gst-tds-tcs).

### TDS you deducted from suppliers

One row per purchase bill on which you ticked **TDS deducted**: **Date**, **Bill No**, **Supplier**, the supplier's **PAN** (read from its GSTIN), **Section**, **Rate**, **Taxable**, **TDS** and what you actually **Paid to supplier** (bill total less TDS). Under the list, **By section** and **By quarter** add them up: these are the figures for your TDS payments and your quarterly TDS return (Form 26Q).

- **Record it on the bill**On the purchase bill, tick **TDS deducted**, pick the section and check the rate (see [TDS on a purchase bill](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html#purchase-tds)).
- **Deposit it**Pay each month's TDS by the 7th of the next month (30 April for March) on the income tax portal, using your TAN.
- **File the return**Pick the quarter here, export to Excel and give it to whoever files your Form 26Q. Then send each supplier its TDS certificate.

You need a TAN (Tax Deduction Account Number) to deduct TDS. Whether you must deduct at all depends on the section and its limits; ask your CA if unsure.

## By cost centre

A cost centre is a branch, a site or a project: "Branch: Jalandhar", "Site A - Ludhiana", "Project Mehta House". Tag your invoices, purchase bills and expenses with one, and this tab shows what each one sold, spent and earned. The feature is off to start.

- **Turn it on.** Settings, Features, under Reports tick **Cost centres**.
- **Add your cost centres.** A **Cost centres** section appears in Settings, under Features. Type a **Name**, an optional **Code**, and click + Add cost centre. Each business has its own list.
- **Tag your documents.** The new invoice form (Invoice Details), the purchase bill form and the expense form get a **Cost centre** box. Pick one, or leave it on **None**. A document has one cost centre; to split one bill between two sites, enter it as two bills.
- **Tag old invoices in one go.** On the Dashboard, tick the invoices, then pick a centre from **Set cost centre…** in the bar that appears. **Remove cost centre** takes it off.
- **Read the report.** Reports, By cost centre. Choose the fiscal year or month at the top (see Choosing the period).

| **Sales (taxable)**, **GST on sales**, **Sales total** | As on the Profit & Loss tab: credit notes are subtracted; cancelled invoices, estimates and challans are left out. |

| **Purchases (ex. GST)** | The taxable value of your purchase bills |

| **Expenses (ex. GST)** | Expenses without their GST |

| **Profit** | Sales (taxable) minus purchases minus expenses. Green for a profit, red for a loss. |

Documents with no cost centre are added up in an **Untagged** row, so the **Total** row is the whole business. Print / PDF, Excel and CSV download the table. Purchase bills have no currency, so they count only when the currency is INR.

### Worked example

Reazix adds two cost centres, **Branch: Ludhiana** (code LDH) and **Project Mehta House**. In April it enters:

- An invoice tagged Branch: Ludhiana: ₹10,000 + 18% GST = ₹11,800.
- An invoice tagged Project Mehta House: ₹20,000 + 18% GST = ₹23,600, and a credit note on it for ₹2,000 + ₹360 GST.
- A purchase bill tagged Project Mehta House: ₹8,000 + 18% GST.
- An expense tagged Branch: Ludhiana: shop rent ₹5,000, no GST.
- One old invoice with no cost centre: ₹1,000 + 18% GST.

| Cost centre | Sales (taxable) | GST on sales | Sales total | Purchases | Expenses | Profit |

| Branch: Ludhiana (LDH) | 10,000 | 1,800 | 11,800 | 0 | 5,000 | 5,000 |

| Project Mehta House | 18,000 | 3,240 | 21,240 | 8,000 | 0 | 10,000 |

| Untagged | 1,000 | 180 | 1,180 | 0 | 0 | 1,000 |

| **Total** | 29,000 | 5,220 | 34,220 | 8,000 | 5,000 | 16,000 |

### Renaming, archiving and filtering

- Edit (pencil) renames a cost centre; reports show the new name.
- Archive takes it out of the **Cost centre** box for new documents. Documents already tagged keep it, and it stays in the lists and in this report, marked **(archived)**, whenever it has something in the period. Restore brings it back. There is no delete, so old documents never lose their tag.
- The Dashboard, Purchases and Expenses lists get an **All cost centres** filter: pick one centre, or **No cost centre** to find what is still untagged.
- The cost centre is not printed on the invoice. Cost centres are part of your backup (they are saved with the settings).
- Turning the feature off hides the boxes, filters and this tab. The tags stay on your documents, and come back when you turn it on again.

**Something wrong?**The By cost centre tab is missing: turn on **Cost centres** in [Settings, Features](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#features) and save, then open Reports again. Most of the money is in **Untagged**: tag the older invoices from the Dashboard (step 4 above) and the purchase bills and expenses from their forms.

---

# Income tax helper

URL: https://billing.reazix.com/help/income-tax.html

Estimate your income tax under the old and new regimes, presumptive taxation (44AD, 44ADA, 44AE), advance tax, bank statement import, and an ITR-4 summary to file from.

**An estimate for one year**
The tax rules built in are for **FY 2025-26** (AY 2026-27). When today is in a later year, a banner says so, and invoices from the later year are not counted: enter that income yourself. Treat every figure as an estimate and have your CA confirm it before filing. The helper does not file your return; see [what it does not do](https://billing.reazix.com/help/limitations.html#income-tax-limits).

## Which year the figures are for

The line under the page title says the year: **FY 2025-26 · AY 2026-27**. **FY** (financial year) is the year you earned the money, 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. **AY** (assessment year) is the year after, when you file the return for it.

If today falls in a later financial year, an amber banner at the top says **These figures are for FY 2025-26, not the current FY ...**. It means:

- The slabs, rebate and capital-gains rates used are those of FY 2025-26. Rates for the newer year are not built in yet, so nothing is worked out with them.
- The business income filled in from your invoices counts only invoices dated in FY 2025-26. Income of the newer year must be typed in by hand.

The banner is a reminder, not an error. You can still use every tab to check FY 2025-26 before filing for it.

## The five tabs

Open Income Tax from the sidebar. The buttons at the top switch between five tabs; rest the mouse on one to see what it does. The small ? at the end of the row opens this guide at the tab you are on.

| Tab | What it does |

| Regime Calculator | Old and new regimes side by side, and which costs less |

| Presumptive (§44AD/ADA) | Income under sections 44AD, 44ADA and 44AE, without full books |

| Advance Tax | The instalments due, and interest for paying late |

| Bank Statement Import | Read a bank CSV and sort each transaction |

| ITR Summary | The year in one place, and the ITR-4 summary PDF |

The tabs work together: the Presumptive tab and the bank import fill the calculator, the calculator's tax drives the Advance Tax tab, and the ITR Summary uses all of them. What you type on the first three tabs is remembered in this browser, so you can close the app and come back. Figures read from your invoices, purchase bills and expenses are for the business selected in the sidebar; what you type stays the same whichever business is selected.

## Regime Calculator

Since FY 2023-24 every individual can choose between two ways of working out income tax:

| | New regime (section 115BAC) | Old regime |

| Rates | Lower slab rates, wider slabs | Higher slab rates |

| Deductions | Almost none: only the standard deduction on salary (₹75,000) and employer NPS, 80CCD(2) | 80C (PPF, LIC, ELSS...), 80D health insurance, home-loan interest, donations and the rest; standard deduction ₹50,000 |

| Zero tax up to | ₹12 lakh of income (rebate under 87A, up to ₹60,000) | ₹5 lakh (rebate up to ₹12,500) |

| How to choose it | The default; nothing to do | Business owners file **Form 10-IEA** before the return's due date |

In short: if you have big deductions (a home loan, full 80C, health insurance for parents), the old regime may cost less; otherwise the new one usually wins. The calculator works out both and tells you.

The left column, **Your income**, is what you type. The right column shows the result, live as you type: the **Recommended** card, then the **Old Regime** and **New Regime** cards side by side.

### Your income

First three questions about you. They change the old-regime slabs and some deduction limits:

| Box | What it changes |

| **Your age on 31 March** | **Under 60**, **60 to 79 (senior citizen)** or **80 or older (super senior citizen)**. Old-regime tax-free limit ₹2.5 lakh, ₹3 lakh or ₹5 lakh. Also the 80D, 80DDB, 80TTA and 80TTB limits. |

| **My parents (whose health insurance I pay) are 60 or older** | Raises the 80D limit for their insurance from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. |

| **I am a government employee** | Employer NPS, 80CCD(2), allowed up to 14% of salary instead of 10%. |

Then your income for the year, in rupees:

| Box | What to enter |

| **Gross Salary (Form 16 box 1)** | Salary before any deduction, as in box 1 of your Form 16. Zero if you have no salary. The standard deduction is applied for you. |

| **Business / Professional Income** | Your business profit. If it is zero, the app fills it in from this business's rupee sales, less purchases and business expenses, all without GST, for FY 2025-26 (personal drawings and asset purchases are not counted as expenses). The note under it then says **Auto-filled from your invoices...**. Change it if your books say otherwise, or use the Presumptive tab. |

| **House Property (rent received)** | Rent from a let-out property, less municipal tax and the 30% standard deduction. Home-loan interest goes in **§24b** below. |

| **Other Sources (bank interest, dividends, etc.)** | Savings and FD interest, dividends, other income. Savings interest also goes in 80TTA below to claim the deduction. |

Reset at the top of the card clears every box on this tab back to zero. (The business income fills itself in again the next time you open the screen.)

**Something wrong?**Business income stays at zero: it is filled only from invoices dated in FY 2025-26, in rupees, for the business selected in the sidebar; and only when the box is zero. Business income looks too high: purchase bills or expenses for the year are not entered in the app. Type the right figure over it.

### Capital gains (special rates)

Profit from selling shares or equity mutual funds is taxed at its own rate, not your slab rate, under both regimes:

| Box | What it is | Tax |

| **STCG on listed equity (§111A)** | Short-term gain: shares or equity funds held 12 months or less | 20% flat |

| **LTCG on listed equity (§112A)** | Long-term gain: held more than 12 months | First ₹1.25 lakh free, 12.5% on the rest |

Gains on property, gold or debt funds are not entered here; ask your CA. With capital gains you may need ITR-2 or ITR-3 instead of ITR-4; see Can you file ITR-4?

### Deductions (Old Regime only)

Each box is an amount you can subtract from income under the old regime. They do **not** reduce new-regime tax. Under each box is its limit (**Cap**) and what it covers; if you type more than the limit, only the limit is counted.

| Box | For | Limit used |

| **§80C** | PPF, ELSS, LIC premium, EPF, children's tuition fees, home-loan principal, NSC | ₹1,50,000 |

| **§80CCD1B** | Your own extra NPS contribution | ₹50,000 |

| **§80D** | Health insurance for self, family and parents | ₹25,000 + ₹25,000; ₹50,000 for each part that is 60 or older |

| **§80TTA** | Savings-account interest, under 60 | ₹10,000 (nothing if 60+) |

| **§80TTB** | Bank and post-office deposit interest, 60 and older | ₹50,000 (nothing if under 60) |

| **§80E** | Education-loan interest, for 8 years | No cap |

| **§80G** | Donations to approved funds and charities | No cap; enter the amount you may claim |

| **§80GG** | Rent you pay when you get no HRA | ₹60,000 |

| **§80DDB** | Treatment of specified serious illness | ₹40,000; ₹1,00,000 if 60+ |

| **§80U** | Your own disability | ₹1,25,000 |

| **§24b** | Home-loan interest on the house you live in | ₹2,00,000 |

| **§80CCD(2) — employer NPS** | What your employer pays into your NPS. Allowed under **both** regimes. | 10% of salary (14% for government employees) |

The 80G box takes the amount you are allowed to claim; the 50% or 100% rule for each charity is not applied for you.

### Recommended regime

The card at the top right says **Recommended: NEW Regime** (green) or **OLD Regime** (purple), and **Saves you ₹... compared to the other regime**. If both cost the same, new is recommended.

- **New recommended**: nothing to do. It is the default when you file.
- **Old recommended**: with business income, file **Form 10-IEA** on incometax.gov.in before the return's due date, or the new regime applies anyway. Salaried people without business income choose in the return itself.

The Advance Tax tab and the ITR Summary use the recommended regime's tax.

### Old Regime and New Regime cards

Each card works out the tax step by step. The recommended one has a coloured border.

| Line | Meaning |

| **Gross Total Income** | Salary after standard deduction, business, house property and other sources added up (capital gains are taxed separately below) |

| **Standard Deduction** | ₹75,000 (new) or ₹50,000 (old) off salary; only if you have salary |

| **Chapter VI-A** | The deductions allowed: all the boxes above for old, only 80CCD(2) for new |

| **Taxable Income** | Income the slabs apply to |

| **Slab Tax** | Tax by the slabs below |

| **STCG (20%)**, **LTCG (12.5%)** | Capital-gains tax, shown only when you entered gains |

| **§87A Rebate** | The tax waived for smaller incomes, shown when it applies |

| **Surcharge** | Extra tax on income above ₹50 lakh, shown when it applies |

| **Health & Ed Cess (4%)** | 4% on the tax plus surcharge |

| **Total Tax** | What you owe for the year, before TDS and advance tax already paid |

The slabs built in, for FY 2025-26:

| New regime | Rate | Old regime (under 60) | Rate |

| Up to ₹4 lakh | 0% | Up to ₹2.5 lakh | 0% |

| ₹4 to 8 lakh | 5% | ₹2.5 to 5 lakh | 5% |

| ₹8 to 12 lakh | 10% | ₹5 to 10 lakh | 20% |

| ₹12 to 16 lakh | 15% | Above ₹10 lakh | 30% |

| ₹16 to 20 lakh | 20% | | |

| ₹20 to 24 lakh | 25% | | |

| Above ₹24 lakh | 30% | | |

For seniors the old regime's 0% band is ₹3 lakh (60 to 79) or ₹5 lakh (80+). The note under the cards, **How this is computed**, gives the order: slabs, then the 87A rebate, then surcharge, then cess.

**Example**A shop owner with ₹10,00,000 business income and no deductions: new regime taxable ₹10 lakh, slab tax ₹40,000, fully waived by the 87A rebate: **₹0**. Old regime: slab tax ₹1,12,500 + 4% cess = **₹1,17,000**. New is recommended.

## Presumptive income

"Presumptive" means the law presumes your profit is a fixed share of your turnover, so you do not keep full books of account or get them audited. You declare that share (or more) as income and file the simple **ITR-4 (Sugam)**. Most small shops, traders and professionals use it.

Fill in the left card (**Section**), check the right card (**Presumptive computation**), then click Use ₹... as Business Income to send the figure to the Regime Calculator.

### Section: 44AD, 44ADA or 44AE

Click the button that fits your work. The boxes below change with it.

| Button | For | Income presumed | Limit |

| §44AD | Trading, retail, wholesale and manufacturing | 6% of turnover received digitally (UPI, NEFT, RTGS, cheque), 8% of cash turnover | ₹3 crore turnover if cash is no more than 5% of it, otherwise ₹2 crore |

| §44ADA | Professionals: CA, doctor, lawyer, architect, engineer, consultant | 50% of gross receipts | ₹75 lakh receipts if cash is no more than 5%, otherwise ₹50 lakh |

| §44AE | Transporters owning up to 10 goods vehicles | ₹1,000 per tonne per month for each heavy vehicle (over 12,000 kg); ₹7,500 per month for each other vehicle | 10 vehicles at any time in the year |

The boxes:

- **44AD**: **Turnover received DIGITALLY (UPI/NEFT/RTGS/cheque)**, **Turnover received in CASH**, and **Actual profit (optional override)**.
- **44ADA**: **Gross receipts (digital)**, **Gross receipts (cash)**, and **Actual profit (optional override)**.
- **44AE**: **Heavy vehicles (> 12,000 kg): sum of vehicle-months** (2 trucks for 12 months = 24), **Heavy vehicle gross tonnage (avg)** (13 to start), and **Light vehicles: sum of vehicle-months**.

**Actual profit**: if your real profit is higher than the presumed share, enter it, because you must declare the higher figure. You cannot declare less than the presumed share under these sections.

- **Find your turnover**Your sales for the year without GST are on the ITR Summary tab (**Sales excl. GST**).
- **Split it**Enter what came by UPI, bank transfer or cheque as digital, and the rest as cash.
- **Check the result**Read the Presumptive computation card and any warning.
- **Send it to the calculator**Click Use ₹... as Business Income.

### Presumptive computation

The right card shows the working:

- 44AD and 44ADA: **Turnover / gross receipts**, **Deemed income @ 6% / 8%** (or **@ 50%**), and **Declared income**: the deemed income, or your actual profit if higher.
- 44AE: **Heavy vehicles (₹1,000 × tonnes × months)**, **Light vehicles (₹7,500 × months)** and **Declared income**.

A yellow box warns when something is wrong: turnover over the limit (you then need regular books, ITR-3 and a tax audit under section 44AB), cash above 5% when that costs you the higher limit, more than 10 vehicles, or an actual profit lower than the presumed share.

Use ₹... as Business Income copies the declared income into **Business / Professional Income** on the Regime Calculator and opens that tab. For 44AD and 44ADA it also ticks **Presumptive** on the Advance Tax tab (pay everything by 15 March). The button is hidden when you are over the limit. The ITR-4 PDF uses this figure for business income.

### Why presumptive taxation?

The box at the bottom right lists what you gain, and the one catch:

- No full books of account and no tax audit (section 44AB).
- Advance tax in one go, by 15 March, instead of four instalments.
- The simple ITR-4 (Sugam) form instead of ITR-3.
- **The catch (44AD):** once you opt in, keep using it for 5 years. If you leave early, you cannot come back to 44AD for the next 5 years.

## Advance tax

Advance tax means paying income tax during the year, in parts, instead of all at the end. If your tax for the year, after TDS already cut, is ₹10,000 or more, you must pay it in four instalments:

| Due by | Paid in total by then |

| 15 June | 15% |

| 15 September | 45% |

| 15 December | 75% |

| 15 March | 100% |

If you use presumptive taxation (44AD or 44ADA), you may pay all of it by 15 March instead. Paying late or short costs interest of 1% a month under sections 234B and 234C. You pay advance tax on incometax.gov.in with challan 280 (e-Pay Tax).

The tab uses the **Total Tax** of the recommended regime from the Regime Calculator, so fill that in first.

### Advance Tax Schedule

The top card. It says **Based on your recommended NEW Regime total tax of ₹...**.

| Item | What it does |

| **Presumptive (pay 100% by 15 March)** | Tick it if you use 44AD or 44ADA: the schedule becomes one instalment on 15 March. |

| **TDS already deducted** | Tax already cut from your salary, interest, rent or contract payments. Find it in Form 26AS or the AIS on incometax.gov.in. |

| **Total tax liability**, **Less: TDS credit**, **Net advance-tax liability** | The tax, the TDS, and what is left to pay as advance tax. |

If what is left is under ₹10,000, a green note says **no advance tax required** and nothing else shows. Otherwise the instalment table appears:

| Column | Meaning |

| **Installment**, **Due Date** | #1 to #4 and their dates |

| **% cumulative** | How much of the year's tax should be paid in total by then |

| **This installment** | The amount for that date alone |

| **Paid by due date** | The payments you entered, dated on or before it |

| **Shortfall** | What is still missing by that date: red if any, green if none |

**Something wrong?**The total tax is zero or wrong: fill in the Regime Calculator first; this tab follows it. A shortfall after you paid: enter the payment, with its real date, under Payments made.

### Payments made

Record each advance-tax payment you have made, so the schedule and the interest are right.

- **Add a line**Click + Add payment. A line appears with today's date.
- **Date**Change it to the date on your challan.
- **Amount**Type what you paid.
- **Remove**The × at the end of a line removes it.

"No advance-tax payments recorded yet." shows until you add one. The payments are remembered in this browser.

### Interest under §234B / §234C

What paying late or short costs, worked out from the schedule and your payments:

- **§234C — installment shortfall**: 1% a month on what was short at each date, for 3 months (1 month for the March instalment). The June and September instalments are forgiven if you paid at least 12% and 36% by then.
- **§234B — post year-end delay (1% per month)**: if by 31 March you had paid less than 90% of the tax, 1% a month on what is unpaid, from 1 April until today.
- **Total interest**: the two added up.

Shortfalls are rounded down to the nearest ₹100 first, as the rules say. The interest is an estimate; the department's figure on filing is final.

## Bank statement import

Turn a year of bank transactions into the figures the calculator needs: interest, rent received, 80C and 80D payments, business receipts.

- **Download a CSV**From net-banking or your bank's app, save the statement for the year as CSV. Excel files must be saved as CSV first; PDFs are not accepted.
- **Drop it in**Drag the file onto the box **Drop a bank-statement CSV here or click to select**, or click it and choose the file. SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, PNB and Yes Bank formats are recognised, and most others with Date, Narration, Debit, Credit and Balance columns work too. It is read on your computer; nothing is uploaded.
- **Check the categories**Each transaction is sorted by its description. Change any that are wrong. Mark your sales receipts as **Business receipts** yourself.
- **Push to the calculator**Click Push to Calculator.

The imported statement is not kept after you leave the screen.

**Something wrong?****"No transactions found"** or **"Could not parse this CSV"**: the file is not the bank's plain CSV, or it is an Excel file renamed to .csv. See [A CSV import did not work](https://billing.reazix.com/help/troubleshooting.html#csv-import).

### How to get the CSV

Shown under the drop box until you import a file:

- **Net-banking**: Accounts, Statements, download as CSV (or as Excel, then open it in Excel and save as CSV).
- **Mobile app**: Account statement, Share, Export CSV.
- Choose the dates of the financial year, 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
- The file is read in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

Import one account at a time. For two accounts, import the first, push it, then import the second and push it.

### Reviewing the transactions

After the import the card is titled with the bank and the count, such as **HDFC — 412 transactions**. Below it, a strip of coloured totals per category, then a table with **Date**, **Description**, **Debit** (red), **Credit** (green) and **Category**.

The app guesses each category from the words in the description; change any by picking from the Category box on its row. The totals follow.

| Category | Guessed from words like | On push |

| Salary income | salary, payroll | Not pushed (enter salary from Form 16) |

| Business receipts | Never guessed: set it on your sales receipts | Added to Business / Professional Income |

| Business expense | office rent, rent paid, EMI, home loan, electricity, broadband, telephone, AWS, Adobe | Not pushed |

| Interest earned | int, interest, SB int | Added to Other Sources, and to 80TTA (up to ₹10,000) |

| Rent received | rent, rental | 70% added to House Property (the 30% deduction taken off) |

| Investment / MF / PPF | SIP, mutual fund, ELSS, PPF, NPS | Not pushed; put 80C items in 80C yourself |

| 80C claim | LIC, life insurance | Added to 80C |

| 80D claim | health insurance, mediclaim | Added to 80D |

| GST paid | GST, CGST, SGST, IGST | Not pushed |

| Transfer / unclassified | IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, and anything not matched | Not pushed |

| Personal spending | Amazon, Flipkart, Swiggy, Zomato, ATM, cash withdrawal | Not pushed |

Push to Calculator **adds** these to what is already in the calculator and opens it. Each statement can be pushed once; pushing again says it is already in the calculator. Import it again to push a fresh copy. Clear throws the imported statement away.

**Something wrong?**Most rows are **Transfer / unclassified**: UPI and NEFT payments carry little description; set the business ones to Business receipts by hand. Figures doubled in the calculator: the same statement was imported and pushed twice; Reset the calculator and push once.

## ITR Summary and the ITR-4 PDF

The whole year in one place, for the business selected in the sidebar. Four cards at the top, for FY 2025-26, all without GST:

| Card | From |

| **Sales excl. GST (FY 2025-26)** | Your rupee invoices, less credit notes; estimates, challans and cancelled invoices left out. TCS is taken out too. |

| **Trading Purchases** | Your [purchase bills](https://billing.reazix.com/help/purchases.html), taxable value |

| **Business Expenses** | Your [expenses](https://billing.reazix.com/help/expenses.html) without GST, except **Personal / Drawings** and **Asset Purchase** |

| **Net Business Income** | Sales less purchases less expenses (never below zero) |

### Income breakdown

Sales, less trading purchases and business expenses, gives **= Net business income**. Then what you typed in the calculator: **+ Salary declared**, **+ Rent received**, **+ Other sources** and **+ Capital gains (STCG + LTCG)**. These last four are greyed when empty.

If you entered expenses under **Asset Purchase** (a computer, a machine, furniture), a note says they are not deducted here: an asset is written off over the years as depreciation (section 32). Ask your CA for the depreciation figure and enter it as a business expense.

The net business income here is from your books. It is not copied into the calculator by itself; the calculator has its own **Business / Professional Income** box.

### Tax snapshot

**Recommended regime**, **Tax under NEW Regime** (or OLD), **Tax under other regime** and **You save vs other regime**, all from the Regime Calculator.

Below, a grey box. If your sales are under ₹2 crore and your [business type](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#business-type) is not professional, it says **You may qualify for Section 44AD presumptive taxation**; see the Presumptive tab. It also gives the due dates: **31 July 2026** for the return when no audit is needed, **31 October 2026** with a tax audit, and the advance-tax dates.

### ITR-4 (Sugam) Filing Summary PDF

Download ITR-4 Summary makes a PDF with each ITR-4 field worked out, in the order of the form, to copy into incometax.gov.in or hand to your CA:

- **Assessee**: business name, GSTIN and PAN from [Settings](https://billing.reazix.com/help/settings.html#company-details).
- **Part A — General**: PAN (or "Fill from your profile"), filing status, Aadhaar reminder.
- **Nature of Business**: the presumptive section and turnover, when you filled the Presumptive tab.
- **B — Income**: salary less standard deduction, house property, business (the presumptive income if you filled that tab, otherwise the calculator's figure), other sources, gross total income.
- **C — Deductions**: each Chapter VI-A deduction under the old regime, or 80CCD(2) under the new.
